deadline_text: Registration for the 2026 session is closed. No application deadline is shown. Next session dates are not posted.
how_to_apply: The page says sign-up is closed for 2026. It does not give application steps. Check the Georgia Tech College of Engineering K-20 initiatives page for the next session.
notes: The same page also describes a separate TryEngineering Summer Institute, a nine day residential program for thirty Georgia high school students at no cost, with no dates given. Georgia residents only.

name: Georgia Work-Based Learning (including Youth Apprenticeship)
org: Georgia Department of Education, Career, Technical and Agricultural Education
what_you_do: This is a state program with four options. Cooperative education is paid. Internship is paid or unpaid. Youth Apprenticeship is paid. Employability Skill Development is for students who already have a job. All of them link school courses to a work site.
who_can_apply: High school students, through their own school's Work-Based Learning coordinator. The state page lists no age or grade rules. Districts set their own (Gwinnett, Fulton County and Cobb above say juniors and seniors age 16 or older).
pay_detail: Co-op and Youth Apprenticeship are paid work-site experiences. Internships may be paid or unpaid.
duration: Varies by option. An Employability Skill Development placement can last up to one school year.
deadline_text: Set by each school or district. No state dates are posted.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's Work-Based Learning coordinator or counselor. Internships can happen only after coursework related to the placement. Co-op students must be enrolled in a course directly related to the job.
notes: Youth Apprenticeship in Georgia is run through the Department of Education and local schools. The Georgia Department of Labor youth page covers work permits and child labor rules only. Georgia Work Ready was not researched. Georgia requires a work permit for students under 16 (see the Georgia Department of Labor work permit page).

name: WorkSource Georgia Youth (WIOA)
org: Technical College System of Georgia, Office of Workforce Development (WorkSource Georgia)
what_you_do: A state youth employment program run through local WorkSource offices. Services listed include tutoring, paid and unpaid work experiences, leadership development, adult mentoring, counseling, financial literacy and GED services.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 24 who face barriers to education, training or employment. Both in-school and out-of-school youth are served. The page does not list the exact barriers or income rules.
pay_detail: Free to join. The services page lists paid and unpaid work experiences, but the pages read give no pay rate.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No application dates listed on the state pages.
how_to_apply: The state pages give no application steps. They give no list of local offices. Use the contact page at tcsg.edu or the WorkSource Georgia portal (worksourcegaportal.com). Find your local office there.
notes: The pages read do not say how to enroll. A call to your local WorkSource office is the real next step. The services page says the Occupational Skills part is for ages 18 to 24. So 14 to 17 year olds would use the other services. Atlanta area teens may also see the city and county programs listed separately in this guide.

name: Teen Gallery Guides @ Getty
org: J. Paul Getty Museum (Getty Center and Getty Villa)
what_you_do: You research artworks. Then you lead tours. You also lead gallery activities for school groups and visitors. This is at the Getty Center or Getty Villa. You build public speaking and teaching skills.
who_can_apply: Sophomores and juniors currently enrolled in high school in Los Angeles County, who are at least 16 when the program starts and live within 25 miles of the Getty Center.
pay_detail: Every intern gets a stipend after finishing the program. Amount not stated. Lunch and transportation to the Getty sites are provided.
duration: Mid-June to early August; interns commit to all program days
deadline_text: The page says the application window typically opens in early February each year. Exact 2027 dates are not posted.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the window opens in early February. Questions: gettyteens@getty.edu.
notes: Supported by the Vera R. Campbell Foundation. The page calls it a paid summer internship but says only that interns receive a stipend. Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.

name: Girls Inc. of Alameda County High School Programs
city: Oakland, CA (and Cal State East Bay, Hayward)
what_you_do: You can join free programs for high school girls. They include coding, with Code the Game for grades 10 to 12. They also include college access and leadership. Some programs offer paid summer internships at Bay Area companies.
who_can_apply: Girls and young women in grades 9 to 12. Programs run at the Simpson Center in Oakland (year-round) and Cal State East Bay in Hayward (summer).
pay_detail: Programs are free to families; internships are paid (rate not posted)
deadline_text: Not posted. Contact Girls Inc.
how_to_apply: Use the Contact Us page at girlsinc-alameda.org. Office: 510 16th St, Oakland. The site does not list application steps.
notes: Code the Game is a six week program (the page mentions a fall offering). Internship pay, hours and ages are not posted.

name: Girls Who Code Clubs and Pathways
what_you_do: You can join a free coding club for grades 3 to 12. It meets after school or on weekends. You can also take the free, self-paced online Pathways program for high school students.
grades: Clubs: grades 3 to 12 (split 3 to 5 and 6 to 12). Pathways: high school.
who_can_apply: Aimed at girls and young women in tech. The page does not spell out the rule for other genders, so ask. Clubs meet 1 to 2 hours a week; Pathways is virtual and self-paced.
pay_detail: Free
duration: 1 to 2 hours per week for Clubs
deadline_text: Ongoing.
how_to_apply: Use Get Started on girlswhocode.com/programs to find a Club or begin Pathways.
notes: The page lists no cohort dates. A separate program for ages 18 to 25 also exists.

name: Glenmont Job Corps Center
org: U.S. Department of Labor Job Corps
what_you_do: Live on campus. You train for a career at no cost. You also earn a high school diploma or equivalent. Training includes nurse assistant. It includes culinary arts and facilities maintenance. HVAC is another. There are more.
who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules, or have other approved status. You must meet background rules. An Admissions Representative reads your application. This person decides if you can join.
pay_detail: Free to students. The campus page lists furnished dorms, meals, basic medical care, books and supplies, and a living allowance paid in cash twice a month.
duration: Not stated on the pages read
deadline_text: No deadline posted. You start by making a MyJobCorps account on the Job Corps website.
how_to_apply: Create a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Finish the application. Then an Admissions Representative sets up an interview. They review your documents and a background check. They also help you pick a campus.
notes: Mostly fits teens 16 and up who are out of school or want a different path. Housing: dorms are listed on the campus page. A center being listed on the Job Corps site does not prove it is enrolling right now, so confirm with an Admissions Representative. The training list above comes from the center's training page and may not be complete. Whether a state work permit applies was not checked.

name: Aspiring Scientists Summer Internship Program (ASSIP)
org: George Mason University, College of Science
what_you_do: You work full time for 8 weeks. You do a one-on-one research project with a George Mason faculty mentor. It can be in person, remote or hybrid. You present at a final poster session.
who_can_apply: High school and undergraduate students. Minimum age 15 by Jun 18, 2026 for remote or computer-lab internships and 16 for in-person wet-lab internships. No minimum GPA; transcripts are not requested.
pay_detail: $25 application fee and, if offered an internship, $1,299 tuition for 3 undergraduate credits. Both can be waived with demonstrated financial need.
duration: 8 weeks, full time (Jun 18 to Aug 12 in 2026)
deadline_text: The 2026 ASSIP Application is now closed. The page posts no date for the 2027 cycle.
how_to_apply: Online application with a personal statement; interested mentors interview strong candidates and offers go out in early April. Request a fee waiver code from cosassip@gmu.edu if needed.
notes: Labs are at the Fairfax campus, the Science and Technology Campus in Manassas, or Woodbridge; students arrange their own transportation and campus housing cannot be arranged for minors. This is a paid-by-the-student internship, not a job, so no work permit.

name: George Mason University High School Dual Enrollment
what_you_do: Take lower-level college courses (100 and 200 level) at George Mason while still in high school and earn college credit. You can take up to 11 credits in one semester.
who_can_apply: Exceptionally talented high school juniors and seniors. You need a non-degree application and fee. You need your official high school transcript. You need permission from your high school counselor or administrator. Non-native English speakers must meet the English proficiency rule.
pay_detail: An application fee and college course costs apply. The amounts are not stated on the page read.
duration: One semester at a time, up to 11 lower-level credits
deadline_text: Deadlines are not stated on the page read. Admission is offered for one semester at a time.
how_to_apply: Complete the Non-Degree application. Send your high school transcript. Send your counselor or administrator's permission. Fairfax County Public Schools and Loudoun County Public Schools students can use the school partnership pages. These are for math and science dual enrollment.
notes: The Admissions Committee may ask for test scores or transcripts from other dual enrollment credits. The page also lists Youth Leadership Conferences and Educational Travel Programs, which were not read in detail.

name: Grafton Job Corps Center
org: U.S. Department of Labor Job Corps
what_you_do: Live on campus. You train for a career at no cost. You also earn a high school diploma or equivalent. Training includes carpentry, electrical and plumbing. It includes certified nurse assistant. There are more.
who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules, or have other approved status. You must meet background rules. An Admissions Representative reads your application. This person decides if you can join.
pay_detail: Free to students. The campus page lists furnished dorms, meals, basic medical care, books and supplies, and a living allowance paid in cash twice a month.
duration: Not stated on the pages read
deadline_text: No deadline posted. You start by making a MyJobCorps account on the Job Corps website.
how_to_apply: Create a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Finish the application. Then an Admissions Representative sets up an interview. They review your documents and a background check. They also help you pick a campus.
notes: Mostly fits teens 16 and up who are out of school or want a different path. Housing: dorms are listed on the campus page. A center being listed on the Job Corps site does not prove it is enrolling right now, so confirm with an Admissions Representative. The training list above comes from the center's training page and may not be complete. Whether a state work permit applies was not checked.

name: Grizzly Youth Academy (National Guard Youth ChalleNGe)
org: California National Guard / California Military Department
city: San Luis Obispo, CA (residential; serves listed central and southern counties)
what_you_do: A free, live in, structured program for teens who are behind in credits or at risk of dropping out. Cadets work on academics, leadership and life skills, and many can earn a GED.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 18 by the first day of class. You must volunteer, since you cannot be forced. You must be credit deficient or at risk of dropping out. You must be a U.S. citizen or legal resident and a California resident. You must be clear of felony charges. You must live in one of these places: Santa Cruz, Santa Clara, Merced, Madera, Fresno, Monterey, San Benito, Kings, Tulare, Inyo, San Luis Obispo, Kern, Santa Barbara or Ventura County, or in Lancaster or Palmdale.
pay_detail: Free to participants (the site says offered free of charge, paid by federal and state partnerships).
duration: Residential phase followed by a long check-in phase. The site's pages disagree on the total length (17.5 months on one page, 5.5 months residential plus 24 months after on another), so ask the academy.
deadline_text: No class start dates or deadlines on the pages read. Start with the online Interest Form and a required virtual orientation.
how_to_apply: Make sure you meet the rules to apply. Fill out the Interest Form on the site. Then watch the required virtual orientation video. It is a must for the application.
notes: Meant for teens who dropped out or are at risk of dropping out. The FAQ says each ChalleNGe program runs its own admissions. Call or write the academy (contact page on its site) about county rules. Many cadets can earn a GED during the residential phase (FAQ). Some counties on the site have no separate region tag in this guide. They are Santa Cruz, Madera, Fresno, Monterey, San Benito, Kings, Tulare, Inyo, San Luis Obispo, Kern and Ventura. Lancaster and Palmdale are in Los Angeles County.

name: High School Summer Internship (Georgia Tech Research Institute)
city: Atlanta, GA; Cobb County; Warner Robins, GA (in person)
what_you_do: Five week paid, in person internship at a Georgia Tech Research Institute site. Interns work up to 24 hours a week on STEM projects with GTRI staff.
who_can_apply: Georgia residents in a public, private, charter or home school in Georgia, in the class of 2027, 2028 or 2029, who are 16 by April 4, 2027 (no exceptions). Proof of U.S. citizenship or U.S. person status is required for most positions. You need your own transportation.
pay_detail: Described as a paid internship. The pay rate is not on the page.
duration: Five weeks, about June 14 to July 23, 2027; up to 24 hours a week, Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
deadline_text: Pre-application launch is planned for December 11, 2026. The closing date is not listed on the page. The page says dates are approximate and final dates will be in the pre-application.
how_to_apply: Complete the online pre-application. It has a resume (PDF), a personal statement and a letter of recommendation. It must be 100% complete before it closes. You can join the 2027 contact registry for updates. Email support.hsi.stem@gtri.gatech.edu with questions.
notes: No weekend, after hours or remote work. Housing is not provided. Do not send unsolicited emails or calls to GTRI employees about internships. The page asks this. Finishing the pre-application does not guarantee a job. Georgia Department of Labor says a work permit is required only for minors who have not reached their 16th birthday. This internship requires age 16 by April 4, 2027.

name: Teen Volunteers and Teen Advisory Council (Gwinnett County Public Library)
what_you_do: Volunteer at a library branch. Your role fits the branch, such as helping with programs or homework help. Teen Advisory Council members meet monthly. They help plan teen activities.
who_can_apply: Age 13 and up. The page says the minimum age is 13 with parental permission required. Homework help covers students in grades K to 12.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering
duration: 40 hours over 6 to 12 months, shifts of 2 to 4 hours
deadline_text: Apply any time. Applications stay on file for six months.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer form from the Apply Online button on the volunteer page. List the branches you want. If you are a GCPS student, use a personal or parent email, not a school email.
notes: The background check on the page applies only to volunteers 18 and older. Open spots vary by branch.

name: Habitat for Humanity East Bay / Silicon Valley: Volunteer
org: Habitat for Humanity East Bay/Silicon Valley
what_you_do: You help build or repair affordable homes on construction sites. Younger teens can help with fundraising, flyers or lunch.
who_can_apply: Age 16 and up for construction sites, even with a parent or guardian. Ages 16 to 18 bring a signed minor waiver. Age 15 and under can help with fundraising, flyers or lunch for site volunteers.
pay_detail: No volunteer fee mentioned on the page
deadline_text: Ongoing. No sign-up deadline stated.
how_to_apply: The page gives no online sign-up link; there is usually a volunteer kiosk on site. Call 866-450-4432 or email Volunteer@HabitatEBSV.org. Groups of 5 or more use the group pages.
notes: Hands-on building experience for age 16 and up. Specific build sites were not listed on the page; ask which are near you.

name: Habitat for Humanity Greater Sacramento: Individual Volunteers (Construction and ReStore)
org: Habitat for Humanity of Greater Sacramento
what_you_do: You help build and repair homes on a job site. Or you work in the ReStore. There you organize, price and stock items. You go to a one hour orientation first. Training, tools and safety gear are provided.
who_can_apply: At least 16 to volunteer on a job site. The page lists no age minimum for the ReStore and no special rules for 16 and 17 year olds. No experience needed.
duration: Shifts Tue to Sat (times not listed)
deadline_text: Rolling. Sign up for shifts after orientation.
how_to_apply: Make a VolunteerHub account (sachabitat.volunteerhub.com), register for and attend a one hour HabiTour orientation, then sign up for shifts. Email volunteers@habitatgreatersac.org or call (916) 440-1215.
notes: Ask whether under-18 volunteers need a parent signature or waiver, since the page does not say. Group volunteering contact: gcabral@habitatgreatersac.org. Office: 819 North 10th St, Sacramento.

name: Hack Club
what_you_do: You can join Hack Club. It is a free teen coding community. It has school clubs and an online Slack. It has game jams, hackathons and hardware events.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18. Free forever for teenagers.
pay_detail: Free
duration: Ongoing
deadline_text: Join anytime.
how_to_apply: Join through hackclub.com and find or start a club.
notes: Free for teens. The page lists about 1,500 clubs and events such as game jams and a hardware hackathon in San Francisco.

name: Hacktoberfest 2026
what_you_do: In October you can join online challenges and livestreams, or go to one of over 500 local in-person fests. This year the event focuses on open source and open-weight AI.
who_can_apply: Open to everyone. The page does not state an age limit. In 2026, pull requests no longer count toward rewards.
pay_detail: Free
duration: All of October 2026
deadline_text: Runs through October 2026; sign in with MyMLH.
how_to_apply: Sign in on hacktoberfest.com with MyMLH, or register for a local fest.
notes: The page states no age limit; check each local fest for age rules. Pull requests no longer count toward rewards in 2026. Earn three stickers to get a sticker pack by mail, and you must sign in with MyMLH and give an address.

name: HandsOn Bay Area Youth Volunteering (HandsOn Tomorrow paused)
what_you_do: You can join monthly volunteer projects for younger volunteers. Find them on the HandsOn Community Calendar. Filter by age to see which are open to you.
grades: High school (for HandsOn Tomorrow and the Youth Council)
who_can_apply: Monthly projects: filter the calendar by age to see which are open to you. HandsOn Tomorrow and the Youth Volunteer Council are for Bay Area high school students; the Council requires finishing HandsOn Tomorrow first.
pay_detail: No cost or pay stated on the pages
duration: Monthly projects; HandsOn Tomorrow was 2 weeks
deadline_text: Monthly projects: sign up on the Community Calendar. HandsOn Tomorrow will not run in summer 2026 and no later dates are posted.
how_to_apply: Use the Community Calendar at handsonbayarea.org/calendar and filter by age. Email info@handsonbayarea.org or call 415-541-9616.
notes: HandsOn Tomorrow, a 2-week summer program (up to 40 hours), is paused and is not running in summer 2026. The Youth Volunteer Council needs HandsOn Tomorrow first, so for now the monthly calendar projects are the way in. Age limits vary by project.

name: ZooTeen Program at Happy Hollow Park and Zoo
org: Happy Hollow Park and Zoo (City of San Jose)
what_you_do: Teens do animal meet-and-greets, help with animal care routines and work as camp helpers. Good for future zookeepers and vet techs.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 17. Animal handling, public speaking or working-with-children experience helps. It is not required.
pay_detail: Unpaid; no cost stated on the page
duration: At least 48 hours a year (about 4 hours a month)
deadline_text: Applications are accepted year-round and reviewed seasonally. The last orientation listed on the page was Oct 18, 2025 (old); no 2026-27 date is posted.
how_to_apply: Download the volunteer application, write a 1-page cover letter about your interests and goals, and send both by mail, email, fax or in person to 1300 Senter Road, San Jose. Selected applicants interview. Phone (408) 794-6425.
notes: Minimum 48 hours a year (about 4 hours a month). Not everyone is picked, but you can reapply the next season.

name: H.A.R.D. Volunteer Program (Hayward Area Recreation and Park District)
org: Hayward Area Recreation and Park District (H.A.R.D.)
what_you_do: Volunteer at district events and ongoing service projects such as senior programs, nature programs, special needs programs and theatre ushering. Teens can earn community service hours and work experience.
who_can_apply: Ages 12 and up. Some jobs have their own age rules, listed on each opportunity. Volunteers under 18 need a parent or guardian to sign the volunteer agreement.
duration: One-time events, or service projects that run 6 months or longer.
deadline_text: Opportunities are posted throughout the year. No closing date is stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Create a volunteer profile, then register for a one-time event or submit an interest form for a service project. Service projects need a background check and TB risk assessment before starting.
notes: This page lists many volunteer roles, not one program, so each role's own age rule applies. Verification of service hours is emailed on request. Volunteers with court orders should follow the district process (info@haywardrec.org).

name: Hayward Public Library Teen Volunteer Opportunities
what_you_do: Teens help the Children's Room librarians with tasks like cleaning books and craft prep, in 1-hour shifts. Teens can also attend Teen Library Council meetings.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17. Library service hours cannot be used for community service required by a judge or court.
duration: Flexible. Volunteers sign up for 1-hour shifts.
deadline_text: Applications are accepted during the school year. No closing date is stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Use the APPLY TO VOLUNTEER online interest form linked from the library page. Questions go to hpl.teens@hayward-ca.gov.
notes: The page says the roles are subject to change, so check the online interest form for current openings. The Just for Teens page describes its events for grades 9-12, while the volunteer page says ages 13-17; the volunteer page is the one used here. An older 2023 city notice describes a monthly Teen Advisory Group meeting (1st Wednesday, Downtown Library, ages 13-17, no commitment). That notice was not re-checked for 2026, so ask hpl.teens@hayward-ca.gov whether it still meets.

name: Hayward Youth Commission
what_you_do: Youth commissioners advise three groups. Those are the Hayward City Council, the Hayward Area Recreation and Park District and the Hayward Unified School District. They advise on issues that affect young people. They also work on youth projects.
who_can_apply: Students ages 13 to 20 who live in the City of Hayward or within the Hayward Unified School District boundaries. Applicants under 18 need a parent or guardian consent form.
duration: Meetings at Hayward City Hall on the second Monday of each month, September to June, except holidays. The 2021 notice said two-year terms.
deadline_text: 2025 cycle: applications due Friday, May 9, 2025. Interviews were on Friday, May 30, 2025. No 2026 cycle was found.
how_to_apply: Get the application and the Parent Agreement and Contact Information form from the City of Hayward website, or call the City Clerk at (510) 583-4400, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. weekdays. Applicants are interviewed by a panel.
notes: The official Youth Commission page returned 404. The newest notice read is from April 2025. The 2021 notice said meetings were on the first and third Mondays, so the meeting schedule may have changed. Confirm the 2026 cycle with the City Clerk before applying.

name: STEAM Squad teen internship
what_you_do: Teen interns work in teams of three. They research and plan activities. They lead science, technology, engineering, art and math activities. These are for kids at participating libraries.
who_can_apply: High school sophomores, juniors and seniors. The page says interns are ages 16 to 18 in one place and 16 to 19 in another.
pay_detail: Described as a hired position; the pay rate is not stated on the page
duration: Year-round (summer and school year), about 6 hours a week after school and weekends
deadline_text: Hiring dates are not stated. Sign up for Hennepin County job notifications to be told about openings.
how_to_apply: Watch Hennepin County job listings (sign up for email notifications from the program page). Libraries hiring interns: Brookdale, Brooklyn Park, Franklin, Hosmer, North Regional, Roosevelt, and Cedar Riverside Opportunity Center.
notes: Training includes hands-on learning, group reflection and an adult mentor. Hiring dates and pay are not on the page. Confirm with the library before relying on it.

name: Teen volunteers
what_you_do: Help at a local Hennepin County library. Positions vary by library.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18. Only a limited number of teen volunteer spots exist at some libraries.
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Ask your local library whether it has a teen opening.
how_to_apply: Ask your local Hennepin County library about teen openings. If there is one, fill out the teen volunteer application (PDF), bring it to the library, and a staff member will contact you. Questions: Volunteer Services, 612-543-8633.
notes: Adult volunteers have a different process. The phone line is staffed Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

name: Hidden Genius Project Immersion Program
what_you_do: You can join a free 15 month program (800+ hours) for Black male high school students. It has two 7-week summers plus a year of after-school sessions in coding, entrepreneurship and leadership.
who_can_apply: Black male students entering grades 9, 10 or 11. No coding experience needed. Must commit to the full 15 months.
pay_detail: Free to join; no stipend listed
duration: 15 months
deadline_text: The application page says applications are currently closed and to follow HGP social media or the newsletter for the 2027 application. The last posted deadline was Feb 21, 2025.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the Immersion Program page on hiddengeniusproject.org.
notes: The immersion page still shows the old 2025 deadline. No 2027 date is posted, so wait for the new announcement. Oakland and Richmond are the East Bay sites.

name: Teen Leadership Council (High Museum of Art)
what_you_do: Join 15 high school students. You learn about art and how a museum works. You talk with artists and tour the collection. You help with public programs. You plan events for other teens.
who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors and seniors enrolled full time in high school for the program year. The group has 15 members.
pay_detail: Described as a paid position; the amount is not stated on the page.
duration: One-year commitment, including a 6-week summer intensive (June 3 to July 17 in 2026), Wednesday to Friday 9:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., plus regular meetings
deadline_text: 2026-27 cycle: applications opened Feb 1 and closed at midnight March 1 (2026); applicants were told by May 1, 2026. The page does not post the 2027-28 cycle.
how_to_apply: Send in the online application during the Feb 1 to Mar 1 window. Questions: HMATeenPrograms@high.org.
notes: No absences are allowed during the summer intensive. The High's Teens and College page also lists an Early College Program in Art History and Curatorial Studies with the Atlanta University Center for rising juniors and seniors, but it gave no dates or application details.

name: Hiller Aviation Museum Flight Teen Volunteers
what_you_do: Teens run hands-on STEM stations like Imagination Playground and virtual reality for visitors on alternating weekend days.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 18. Application, interview, orientation and hands-on training.
pay_detail: Unpaid; no cost stated on the page
duration: Alternating Saturdays or Sundays (1st and 3rd, or 2nd and 4th), plus an extra shift on a 5th weekend some months
deadline_text: Applications are accepted on an ongoing basis.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Flight Teen application online, then expect a call to schedule an interview, attend volunteer orientation, and train with an active volunteer.
notes: Year-round, ongoing applications. Weekend shifts only. Interview timing and training length are not stated.

name: Hire LA's Youth
org: City of Los Angeles Economic and Workforce Development Department (EWDD)
what_you_do: Get a starter job with work-skills training, career coaching and money lessons. One sub-program puts high school students to work helping elementary kids in LA's BEST after-school programs.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 24 living in the City of Los Angeles. The checklist PDF we read (2024 version) lists the other rules on who can join. Check the current one.
pay_detail: Paid. The home page does not state an hourly rate.
duration: Varies. Student to Student Success is up to 140 hours in one school semester (20 hours of training, up to 120 hours of service).
deadline_text: The site banner says it is accepting applications but gives no dates, and its document library page still shows a 2022 summer banner. Call EWDD at 213-744-7300 to confirm the current cycle.
how_to_apply: Create an application on the Hire LA site, then bring or upload proof of age, right-to-work (I-9) documents, City of LA residency and the family income form.
notes: Cycle dates are not confirmed, so check with EWDD before counting on a summer 2027 spot. The same city department runs 14 free YouthSource Centers for ages 14 to 24 (school help, job readiness, some paid internships); ask at your nearest center, for example Boyle Heights 323-526-5800 or South LA 323-903-6926. Under 18 you need a California work permit. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.

name: Hoag Jr. Auxiliary / Candystripers (High School Volunteer)
what_you_do: You greet visitors in the lobby. You escort people. You work in the gift store. You help in the cancer center infusion area. Duties are limited because volunteers are minors.
who_can_apply: Local students ages 16 to 18. No grade level is stated.
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: The program is full. The page says to check back January 2027 for when interest forms will be taken again.
how_to_apply: The page lists no application or interest form for this program. Call the Volunteer Office to ask when interest will be taken again.
notes: Not offered: summer, short-term, hands-on patient care, shadowing or observation. Volunteer Office phones: Newport Beach (949) 764-8264, Irvine (949) 517-3152. Specific weekly hours are not stated on the page.

name: Holy Cross Health volunteer program (high school students)
org: Holy Cross Health (Silver Spring and Germantown hospitals)
what_you_do: Volunteer in a Holy Cross hospital or health center in a clinical, customer service, administrative or support role. Year-round and summer-only openings are listed.
who_can_apply: Minimum age is 16. High school students use a separate application and must attend an in-person orientation. Needs a health screening (MMR, varicella, flu, TB testing) and availability to start within one month of applying.
pay_detail: Unpaid.
duration: Not stated on the main page
deadline_text: No deadline stated.
how_to_apply: Submit the application form for high school students from the Holy Cross volunteer applications page, then complete a screening interview and orientation.
notes: Another site named holy-cross.com is Holy Cross in Fort Lauderdale, Florida; use holycrosshealth.org for Maryland. Background checks are required for volunteers 18 and older. Unpaid volunteering, so no work permit.

name: HOSA Future Health Professionals
what_you_do: You can join this student group for health science students. It has skills contests, leadership events and health career exploration.
grades: Secondary and college students (exact grades not stated)
who_can_apply: Students in health science or biomedical science programs, or interested in health careers. Join through a school chapter.
pay_detail: Dues were not stated on the page. Ask your advisor.
duration: School year
deadline_text: Join through your health science teacher.
how_to_apply: Ask your health science teacher for the chapter advisor.
notes: HOSA reports over 200,000 members in 51 chartered associations. California chapter rules, dues and middle school eligibility were not on the page.

name: Humane Society Silicon Valley Student Volunteer Program
what_you_do: Students under 18 can foster cats or dogs at home. They need a parent or guardian with them. They can also make no-sew fleece blankets for shelter animals. You earn service hours.
who_can_apply: On-site animal care volunteers must be 18 or older. Students under 18 can foster with a parent or guardian's support or make fleece blankets.
pay_detail: Unpaid; no cost stated. HSSV provides foster supplies.
deadline_text: Rolling.
how_to_apply: Email volunteer@hssv.org or see the student opportunities page for fostering and blanket instructions.
notes: No hands-on shelter work until 18. Service hours: 2 fleece blankets = 1 hour (0.5 hour each); fostering is counted by care time. Email for a service hour verification letter.

name: Huntington Beach Public Library Teen Volunteering
what_you_do: Pick a library role. Choices include tech helper, LEGO Club assistant and seed library packer. You can also help with a chess or D&D club. You can also do general branch help like crafts, cleaning and setup.
who_can_apply: Most roles are ages 13 to 17 (18-year-olds still in high school can also join). Teen Tech Volunteer is ages 15 to 17, Chess Club Volunteer is ages 15 to 18 in high school, and Helen Murphy toy cleaning is 13 and up. D&D Club volunteers must have attended a club meeting in the past six months.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Sessions earn 1 to 3 volunteer hours.
duration: Varies by role: weekly or monthly sessions of 1 to 3 hours
deadline_text: Most roles take online applications with no deadline. The Teen Tech role lists applications Aug 29 to Sep 12 and interviews Sep 15 to 18, but the page gives no year, so check the date.
how_to_apply: Use the online application for the role you want (several library roles share one application link, so check which one). Seats for club roles are first-come, first-served, and staff email next steps. The Main Street Branch also accepts a printed teen application dropped off at the branch.
notes: Contact: Teen Services Librarian Katelyn Wong (Katelyn.Wong@surfcity-hb.org) or the library at 714-842-4481. The page also lists other Huntington Beach volunteer groups for teens (Bolsa Chica Conservancy, Bolsa Chica Land Trust, Shipley Nature Center, OC Coastkeeper cleanups) with their own age rules, so read it for those. Some entries on the page look copy-pasted, so confirm details with staff.

name: Illinois 4-H clubs and teen leadership teams
what_you_do: Join a local 4-H club and pick projects. Older teens can also join state teen teams, like STEM Ambassadors, Healthy Living Ambassadors or the Youth Leadership Team.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 8 to 18 join a 4-H Club. Your age on September 1, the start of the 4-H year, decides how you join. Teen teams: Creative Collective Art Ambassadors is ages 14 to 18, and Illinois 4-H Influencers is for high school age youth. Other teams do not list ages on the page.
pay_detail: Fees are not stated on the page. Ask your local Extension office.
duration: 4-H year starts September 1. Teen team terms are about one year (stated for the Art Ambassadors).
deadline_text: No sign-up deadline is posted. Teen team applications and dates are not posted on the main teen page.
how_to_apply: Fill out the form on the Join 4-H page with a parent or guardian. Your local Extension office then contacts you with next steps to register. Returning members renew in Zsuite.
notes: This is club membership and volunteer leadership, not a paid job. Cost, grades and teen team application steps are not stated on the pages read. Call Illinois 4-H at (217) 333-0910 or email Illinois4H@illinois.edu.

grades: High school juniors (finished at least one semester of 11th grade)
name: Illinois Boys State (American Legion)
what_you_do: This is a week-long program. Young men run a mock state government on the Eastern Illinois University campus. There are scholarship contests. You also get lifelong alumni membership.
who_can_apply: Boys who have completed one semester of 11th grade and have at least one semester left after Boys State. Those who finished junior year get preference. A boy may attend only once as a citizen. Many are sponsored by a local American Legion post.
pay_detail: $400 registration fee covering program, up to 10 scholarship contests, housing and meals. Most delegates are sponsored by a local American Legion post.
duration: One week, June 12 to 18, 2027 (90th annual session)
deadline_text: The registration page says registration for the 2027 session closes at 4:00 PM on June 12, 2027, when the session starts. Ask your local Legion post about its earlier sponsor deadline.
how_to_apply: Complete the online registration form; your local American Legion post will then contact you. Parents can also register eligible sons. Questions: info@illinoisboysstate.org or 309-663-0361.
notes: Boys only. Delegates must stay all week and may not drive or leave campus. The Samsung Scholarship application must be finished before arriving.

name: Illinois DECA chapters and state conference
org: Illinois DECA (chartered association of DECA Inc.)
what_you_do: Join a DECA chapter to practice business skills in marketing, management, entrepreneurship, hospitality and tourism, or finance. Chapters compete at an Illinois state conference each spring.
who_can_apply: Members must have an interest in marketing, management, entrepreneurship, hospitality and tourism or finance. A chapter needs a certified local educator as advisor. Grades and ages are not listed on the pages read.
pay_detail: $17 per member: $9 to the state association plus $8 to DECA Inc. Chapters may add local fees (not stated).
duration: School year
deadline_text: The Illinois DECA conference is March 4 to 6, 2027 at the Hyatt Regency O'Hare in Rosemont, IL. No membership deadline is posted.
how_to_apply: Ask your school for a DECA chapter and advisor. If your school has none, the Illinois DECA site has a Start a Chapter page. Membership runs through the DECA membership portal linked on ildeca.org.
notes: Not a paid job. Dues and conference dates come from the DECA Inc. page for Illinois. The state site ildeca.org did not repeat them. Mailing address on the state site: 2460 Dundee Road, Box 1001, Northbrook, IL 60065.

name: ALA Illini Girls State (American Legion Auxiliary)
org: American Legion Auxiliary Department of Illinois
city: Illinois (location not stated on the site)
what_you_do: A week-long citizenship and leadership program for high school girls, sponsored by an American Legion Auxiliary Unit. Delegates must attend the full session.
who_can_apply: High school girls who are current juniors. A principal, guidance counselor or home school administrator must certify leadership qualities, good character and U.S. residency. You must secure sponsorship from an American Legion Auxiliary Unit and attend an orientation.
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the pages we read. Ask the Illinois Girls State office and your local American Legion Auxiliary unit.
duration: One week, June 20 to 26, 2027
deadline_text: Next session is June 20 to 26, 2027. The application deadline is not stated on the pages read; contact the Department office.
how_to_apply: Complete the online registration form (name, school email, counselor name and email, school, hometown), get approval from your school official, find a sponsoring American Legion Auxiliary Unit and attend an orientation. Call 309-663-9366 or email info@alaigs.org.
notes: Girls only. The program is physically active with long walks; the registration page asks you to check with a doctor if you have limits. After the program you share your experience with your sponsoring Unit.

name: SRELO summer research at IMSA
org: Illinois Mathematics and Science Academy (IMSA), Aurora
city: Aurora, IL (open to Illinois students statewide)
what_you_do: Spend two weeks on a research project with an IMSA faculty mentor. The 2026 projects included AI and cardiology or neuroscience, molecular modeling, Chinese history and building a game in Pygame.
who_can_apply: Rising 11th and 12th graders who are Illinois residents. You need earlier research experience (a research program, course or science fair). If you do not have it, you must finish an online Research Fundamentals course first.
pay_detail: No pay and no program cost are stated. The Research Fundamentals course has a fee that is refunded when you finish the course and program. A need-based scholarship exists for that course.
duration: Two weeks. In 2026 the sessions ran June 1 to 12, June 15 to 26 and July 6 to 17.
deadline_text: The 2026 application portal showed closed. No 2027 dates are posted. Sessions in 2026 were in June and July.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application form linked on the IMSA page when the portal opens. Questions go to Dr. Anita White at awhite@imsa.edu or 630-907-5949.
notes: Residential students live in IMSA halls and get all meals. Commuters get breakfast and lunch but must drive to the Aurora campus. Topics change each year.

name: ISBE Student Advisory Council
what_you_do: Research education topics that affect Illinois public school students. Meet with policymakers and community partners, then present policy ideas to the State Board of Education.
who_can_apply: Students who are a sophomore, junior or senior at a charter or public high school in Illinois. You must be in that grade during the year you apply.
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the page.
duration: One school year. Members meet several times a month, online and in person.
deadline_text: The 2026-27 application closed June 30, 2026 and late applications were not considered. Finalists were emailed in July for a video interview.
how_to_apply: Make a Submittable account with a personal email, not a school email. Then send in the online application. Finalists do a video interview. Returning members apply again. They skip the interview.
notes: The ISBE page is marked archived, so watch the page for the next call for applications. Next year's dates are not posted; the June 30 date is from the last cycle.

name: Civil Air Patrol cadets, Illinois Wing
what_you_do: Cadets fly, learn to lead, hike, camp and get in shape. Squadrons meet about 2.5 hours a week plus about one Saturday a month, with summer encampments and career academies.
who_can_apply: You must be at least 12 years old and not yet 19. Members under 18 join a cadet or composite squadron, not a senior squadron.
pay_detail: Dues and uniform costs are not stated on the pages read. Ask the squadron.
duration: Weekly meetings all year
deadline_text: No deadline. Join any time through a local squadron.
how_to_apply: Find your local squadron with the unit locator or the Illinois Wing units page. Contact the unit to confirm a meeting. You usually go to about three meetings. Then you finish the membership application.
notes: Volunteer youth program, not a job. The national page says ages 12 to 18; the Illinois page says at least 12 and not yet 19. Illinois Wing HQ: 630-524-4400 or wa@ilwg.cap.gov.

name: Illinois YMCA Youth and Government
city: Springfield, IL (state conference), delegations across Illinois
what_you_do: Join a delegation and take a role in a student model of Illinois state government. Roles include legislator, attorney, lobbyist or press team. You use what you learn at a state conference.
who_can_apply: High school students. Legislative Assistant and Press Team are open to freshmen through seniors. Lobbyist and Attorney are for sophomores to seniors. Legislator is for juniors and seniors. Anyone can be a Clerk-Bailiff.
pay_detail: $455 program fee. Your delegation decides how it is collected (full payment, deposit, or register first). Scholarships are available through the registration application.
duration: School year, ending with a state conference
deadline_text: The scholarship portal closes October 1, 2026 and scholarship decisions come before November 1. Conference dates and a general registration deadline are not posted on the page read.
how_to_apply: Get the registration link from your local Delegation Advisor. A student and a parent or guardian both sign the code of conduct. You pick a preferred role and give your State Senator and State Representative. Contact the state office if you have no delegation.
notes: Not a job. State office: 1315 Butterfield Rd, Suite 218, Downers Grove, IL 60515, (630) 833-9622, ilyag@ilymcayg.org.

name: Indiana DECA chapters and state conference
org: Indiana DECA (chartered association of DECA Inc.)
what_you_do: Join a DECA chapter at a school with business or marketing classes. Members build business skills. They compete at the Indiana state conference.
who_can_apply: Members must be in a business or marketing class now or have been before. The Indiana Department of Education must recognize chapters. They must have business courses. Grades and ages are not listed.
pay_detail: $15 per member: $7 to the state association plus $8 to DECA Inc. Local chapter fees are not stated.
duration: School year
deadline_text: The Indiana DECA conference is February 26 to 28, 2027 at the Indianapolis Marriott Downtown. No membership deadline is posted.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's business or marketing teacher. Ask about joining or starting a DECA chapter. Send state questions to the Indiana DECA advisor. Use indianadeca@gmail.com.
notes: Not a paid job. The state website listed on the page is indianadeca.org. This card is based on the DECA Inc. page for Indiana.

name: WorkOne young adult (youth) services
org: Indiana Department of Workforce Development, WorkOne Career Centers
city: Statewide, with WorkOne centers in Lafayette and other Indiana cities
what_you_do: Career advising and job-readiness help for young people through WorkOne centers. Pay or work placements are not described on the page; ask the center what is offered.
who_can_apply: The state page says in-school young adults ages 14 to 21 and out-of-school young adults ages 16 to 24 may be eligible. Eligibility rules beyond age are not stated.
pay_detail: Cost and pay are not stated on the page. Ask the program before you count on either.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No deadline posted. Contact a WorkOne center.
how_to_apply: Connect with your local WorkOne Career Center (Lafayette office serves Tippecanoe County; schedule by appointment through the WorkOne West Central site). Ask about the young adult program.
notes: This is the state workforce agency's WIOA-style youth help, not a single job. The WorkOne West Central about page (older) says a youth program for ages 16 to 24 is offered; the newer state page says 14 to 21 in school. The Bloomington (South Central) WorkOne regional page was not read, so confirm locally. Call before going. Re-read on 2026-10-09: the state page says nothing about cost or pay, so the card is not in the paid group.

name: Indiana FFA membership through your school ag class
what_you_do: Join FFA through your school's agriculture class. FFA is the student group tied to agricultural education in Indiana. Local chapters run the activities.
who_can_apply: To join FFA, you must be enrolled in an agriculture course at your school. The page does not list grades or ages.
pay_detail: State dues are $14 per active member per year (includes national, state and district dues). Local chapters set their own local dues.
duration: School year
deadline_text: Indiana FFA says affiliation declarations are due October 1, rosters November 1 and student test numbers December 1. These are chapter deadlines for the teacher.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school counselor or agriculture teacher about enrolling in an agricultural education class. The Indiana Agricultural Education site explains how to start a program if your school has none.
notes: Not a job. Your school needs an ag class and an FFA chapter. The page links the Indiana Agricultural Education program for how to start one.

name: Hoosier Boys State
org: American Legion, Department of Indiana (Hoosier Boys State, Inc.)
what_you_do: For one week, build a mock Indiana state government. Delegates form two made-up parties, run for office, propose laws, negotiate bills and meet real officials.
who_can_apply: Boys going into their senior year of high school. No age limit is listed on the page.
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the pages read. The About page lists scholarships for college. Bring no more than $30 spending money.
duration: One week
deadline_text: Registration opens January 11, 2027. The 2027 session is June 13 to 18, 2027. No registration deadline is posted.
how_to_apply: Registration opens January 11, 2027 on the Hoosier Boys State site. The application steps are not described on the pages read. Email info@hoosierboysstate.org or call 317-630-1301.
notes: The FAQ on the About page says the cost to attend is $400. The About page says a $50 non-refundable application fee is due, and the remaining $350 sponsorship fee is paid by a local American Legion Post or other community partner. Drop-off and pickup is at the MTI Center, 1215 Thunder Ave, Angola, IN. Not a job. The page links to a separate Girls State site (alahgs.org) that returned a 404, so no Hoosier Girls State card was written.

name: Civil Air Patrol cadets, Indiana Wing
what_you_do: Learn leadership, aerospace, fitness and character in a year-round cadet squadron. Cadets wear uniforms, learn drill, earn promotions and plan activities. You do not have to join the military.
who_can_apply: Be at least 12 and not yet 19. You must be a U.S. citizen or a lawful permanent resident (national headquarters may waive this for some non-citizens). Cadets can stay in until their 21st birthday.
pay_detail: Dues and fees are not stated on the pages read. The application lists payment options.
duration: Weekly meetings all year, plus a summer encampment
deadline_text: No deadline. Join any time through a local squadron.
how_to_apply: Find a cadet or composite squadron with the locator. Visit a meeting with your parents. Go to at least three weekly meetings. Then complete the application. Some squadrons take it online.
notes: Volunteer youth program, not a job. Indiana Wing office: 4760 Andrews St, Columbus, IN 47203, 877-350-8643, info@inwg.cap.gov.

name: Indiana YMCA Youth and Government (INYaG)
org: Indiana YMCA Youth and Government (Alliance of Indiana YMCAs)
city: Indianapolis, IN (state conference), delegations across Indiana
what_you_do: Learn how government works by acting it out. Delegates research and debate public issues. They take mock legislative, executive and court roles. Then they serve as delegates at the state conference.
who_can_apply: Hoosier students in 6th through 12th grade.
pay_detail: Program fees are not listed on the page read. Ask the program contact.
duration: School year, ending with a state conference
deadline_text: 2026-27 conference and registration dates are not posted on the page read (it links only a 2024-2025 calendar).
how_to_apply: Contact Shelby Lashbrook. Use shelby@indianaymcas.org or (317) 715-2145. Do this to join, start a delegation, volunteer or sponsor.
notes: Not a job. Office: 6610 N Shadeland Ave, Indianapolis, IN 46220, open Monday to Friday 8:30 am to 4:30 pm.

name: Inova high school student volunteer sessions
city: Fairfax, Alexandria and Northern Virginia hospitals, VA
what_you_do: You volunteer one 3 to 4 hour shift a week at an Inova hospital. You can pick a spring, summer or fall session. You learn about patient care, retail and operations.
grades: High school (through the summer after graduation)
who_can_apply: Must be at least 16 by the start of the session, interested in a healthcare career, and able to attend every session date. Needs a 250-word written response, background check, TB screening, MMR, varicella and Tdap proof, an interview with a parent, an in-person orientation and photo ID.
pay_detail: Unpaid.
duration: Spring 2027 session: Jan 4 to Jun 20, 2027; 1 shift per week, 3 to 4 hours
deadline_text: Spring 2027 registration opens Nov 5, 2026 at 4 p.m. and closes Nov 8, 2026 at 11:45 p.m. Inova also runs summer and fall sessions.
how_to_apply: Register during the window through the 'High school students register here' link on Inova's student page. Spots are assigned by lottery, one entry per applicant, and the student handles all email.
notes: Mandatory student-and-parent info meetings are in mid-November 2026 and orientations in late December 2026 (dates differ by hospital; one of each is required). Unpaid volunteering, so no work permit.

name: Iroquois Job Corps Center
org: U.S. Department of Labor Job Corps
what_you_do: Live on campus and train for a career at no cost. You also earn a high school diploma or equivalent. Training includes bricklayer, carpentry, electrical, painting and more.
who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules, or have other approved status. You must meet background rules. An Admissions Representative reads your application. This person decides if you can join.
pay_detail: Free to students. The campus page lists furnished dorms, meals, basic medical care, books and supplies, and a living allowance paid in cash twice a month.
duration: Not stated on the pages read
deadline_text: No deadline posted. You start by making a MyJobCorps account on the Job Corps website.
how_to_apply: Create a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Finish the application. Then an Admissions Representative sets up an interview. They review your documents and a background check. They also help you pick a campus.
notes: Mostly fits teens 16 and up who are out of school or want a different path. Housing: dorms are listed on the campus page. A center being listed on the Job Corps site does not prove it is enrolling right now, so confirm with an Admissions Representative. The training list above comes from the center's training page and may not be complete. Whether a state work permit applies was not checked.

name: Irvine Public Library Teen Volunteers
what_you_do: You help library staff with programs and crafts. You also help with the seed library and toy cleaning. You can help run the Summer Reading Program. Or join the Teen Advisory Group (TAG) for service projects. TAG also gives feedback on teen programs.
who_can_apply: High school students ages 14 and over (program assistance and toy cleaning are ages 14 to 17). Teen Summer Reading volunteers are students in grades 8 to 11. Each library has up to 20 TAG memberships.
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Summer Reading volunteers work a weekly two-hour shift. Other roles vary.
deadline_text: The undated page says: Summer Reading applications ran May 9 to May 30, school-year roles reopen Saturday, August 1, and TAG is full with a wait list for applications after August 26. No year is shown, so confirm current openings.
how_to_apply: Submit the Teen Volunteer Application on the library's volunteer system at www.volgistics.com/appform/337674493. A required orientation comes before the summer program.
notes: The page lists no library contact; it points to the volunteer coordinator, and the City of Irvine main number is 949-724-6000. The page writes the Teen Volunteer Application link as volgistics.com/appform/337674493 and links it over https, so apply_url uses https.

name: JA Launchpad (Junior Achievement, Fremont)
what_you_do: You will be able to join a new career center in Fremont, coming in early 2027. It offers a money-management simulation, a student business program and career summits with company mentors.
who_can_apply: Students in Northern California; grade levels not stated. The center is not open yet.
pay_detail: Free to students (page says programs are delivered at no cost)
deadline_text: The page says the center is Coming Early 2027. No opening date or sign-up is posted.
how_to_apply: No sign-up steps yet. Call JA of Northern California at (925) 465-1070.
notes: Not open yet, and the page lists no registration steps or opening date. Watch for it in early 2027. The contact on the page is for sponsors and partners.

name: Teen Advisory Board (TAB)
what_you_do: Teens meet monthly at a branch. They suggest teen programs and library materials. They work on group projects. They earn volunteer credit.
who_can_apply: Ages 11 to 18 (students in 6th grade or older). Boards meet at Central (1st Monday, 5 pm), Greene County, Louisa County, Nelson Memorial and Northside; Crozet is full and Gordon Avenue is not currently running.
duration: One meeting a month
deadline_text: No deadline stated.
how_to_apply: Use the Join a Teen Advisory Board page or contact your branch. The page does not say how to apply beyond that.
notes: Meeting times: Greene 1st Tuesday 4-5 pm; Louisa 3rd Thursday 3:45 pm; Nelson 2nd Thursday 4-5 pm; Northside 2nd Monday 7-8 pm. Gordon Avenue's entry on the teen volunteers page says its board is accepting applications while the TAB page says it is not currently running; call the branch.

name: Teen Volunteers at JMRL
what_you_do: Teen volunteers prepare program and distribution materials. They make displays and set up meeting rooms. They help with the summer reading program at a library branch.
who_can_apply: Anyone at least 13 years old. Teen volunteers should be able to work independently. Branches include Central, Crozet, Gordon Avenue, Greene County, Louisa County, Nelson Memorial, Northside and Scottsville.
duration: Varies by branch
deadline_text: The page gives a cutoff date for summer volunteer applications of 5/28/26 and does not say which branches it covers.
how_to_apply: Contact your local branch (Send a Message link) or email the Young Adult Services Manager through the JMRL contact form. The page does not list formal application steps.
notes: Volunteering can count toward school or club service requirements. At the time of reading, Gordon Avenue said all weekly positions were filled. JMRL's volunteer coordinator is listed as Acacia Rodgers, volunteer@jmrl.org, 434-979-7151 ext 6695.

name: Job Corps (Brunswick and Turner centers, Georgia)
org: U.S. Department of Labor Job Corps
what_you_do: Free career training campus. The Georgia center pages list trades like construction and electrical pre-apprenticeships, bricklaying, carpentry, asphalt paving and Certified Nurse Assistant.
who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. The national site says you must be low income. You must meet citizenship, residency or other approved status rules. You must meet background rules. You must be ready and motivated to succeed. The pages read do not explain rules for applicants under 18.
pay_detail: Free. The national site says it covers housing, meals, basic medical care and a living allowance. The living allowance amount is not stated on the pages read.
duration: Not stated on the pages read
deadline_text: Open enrollment: you can start at any time. The application process usually takes about two months.
how_to_apply: Go to enroll.jobcorps.gov. Make a MyJobCorps account. Upload the documents that show you are eligible. Then have an interview with an admissions representative. Call 800-733-5627 with questions.
notes: Brunswick center: 4401 Glynco Pkwy, Brunswick, GA 31525. Turner center: 2000 Schilling Ave, Albany, GA 31705. Neither center page showed a closure notice on 2026-10-09. The application asks for ID, Social Security number and proof of income. That is normal for this federal program, but only enter it on the official jobcorps.gov site with a parent or guardian. A parent should ask an admissions representative about the rules for 16 and 17 year olds. The Atlanta center is not listed here because its page could not be confirmed.

name: Job Corps: Hubert H. Humphrey Job Corps Center
org: U.S. Department of Labor Job Corps
what_you_do: Free live-on-campus career training. The center lists Advanced Transportation Service Worker, Building Construction Technology (pre-apprentice), Culinary Arts and Office Administration.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 through 24. You must be low income. You must meet citizenship, residency or other approved status rules. You must meet background rules. You must be ready and motivated. The pages read do not explain parent consent for applicants under 18.
pay_detail: Training is free. The national site lists free housing, meals, basic medical care and a living allowance. The allowance amount is not stated on the pages read.
duration: Not stated on the pages read
deadline_text: Open enrollment: you can start the application at any time.
how_to_apply: Go to enroll.jobcorps.gov. Make a MyJobCorps account. Fill out the application. Upload the papers that show you are eligible. Examples are proof of income and proof of citizenship or residency. Then have an interview with an admissions representative. Call 800-733-5627 with questions.
notes: Address: 1480 Snelling Ave N, St. Paul, MN 55108. Job Corps is a training program, not a job. After applying, the national site says the review includes a background check (1 to 2 weeks) and a campus review (about 30 days).

name: Job Corps Sacramento Center
org: U.S. Department of Labor Job Corps
what_you_do: You can get free live-in career training. Choose construction, carpentry, cement masonry or Certified Nurse Assistant. You also get help finishing high school. You can earn a high school equivalency.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24 who are low income and meet citizenship, residency or other approved status rules, plus background checks (per the national Job Corps site). Mostly fits teens who are out of school or want a different path. Housing is on campus.
pay_detail: Free tuition, housing, meals and basic medical care, plus a monthly living allowance (amount not stated).
deadline_text: Ongoing enrollment. No dates posted on the Sacramento page.
how_to_apply: Apply at enroll.jobcorps.gov or call 800-733-JOBS (800-733-5627).
notes: Residential, so you live on campus at 3100 Meadowview Rd, Sacramento. The Sacramento page lists the trades (building construction, carpentry, cement masonry, Certified Nurse Assistant) but not the age or income rules, which come from jobcorps.gov. A federal settlement reported Aug 12, 2026 kept all 99 centers open, but that article does not name Sacramento, so confirm the center is enrolling.

name: Job Corps: Gary Job Corps Center (San Marcos)
org: U.S. Department of Labor Job Corps
what_you_do: Free live-on-campus career training. Programs listed include Advanced Cement Masonry (Pre-Apprentice), Advanced Electrical (Overhead Line Construction) and Advanced Transportation Service Worker.
who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must be low income. You must meet citizenship, residency or other approved status rules. You must meet background rules. You must be ready and motivated. The page does not explain rules for applicants under 18.
pay_detail: Training is free. The national site lists free housing, meals, basic medical care and a living allowance. The allowance amount is not stated on the pages read.
duration: Not stated on the pages read
deadline_text: Open enrollment: you can start the application at any time.
how_to_apply: Go to enroll.jobcorps.gov. Click Apply Now. Make a MyJobCorps account. Upload eligibility papers. Then have an interview with an admissions representative. Or call 800-733-5627.
notes: The center page footer lists 2800 Airport Hwy 21 E, San Marcos, TX 78667. Job Corps is a training program, not a job. Texas has other Job Corps centers that are not covered by this card.

name: Job Corps (Cascades, Curlew and Columbia Basin centers, Washington)
org: U.S. Department of Labor Job Corps
city: Sedro-Woolley, Curlew and Moses Lake, WA
what_you_do: Free live-on-campus career training. Centers list computer and medical assistant, carpentry, cement masonry, human services, fire management and nursing assistant training.
who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must be low income. You must meet citizenship, residency or other approved status rules. You must meet background rules. You must be ready and motivated. The pages read do not explain rules for applicants under 18.
pay_detail: Training is free. The national site lists free housing, meals, basic medical care and a living allowance. The allowance amount is not stated on the pages read.
duration: Not stated on the pages read
deadline_text: Open enrollment: you can start the application at any time.
how_to_apply: Go to enroll.jobcorps.gov. Click Apply Now. Make a MyJobCorps account. Upload the papers that show you are eligible. Then have an interview with an admissions representative. Phone for Curlew and Columbia Basin: 877-763-0580.
notes: Addresses: Cascades, 2060 Powerhouse Drive, Sedro-Woolley, WA 98284. Curlew, 3 Campus St, Curlew, WA 99118. Columbia Basin, 6739 24th Ave NE Bldg 2402, Moses Lake, WA 98837. Job Corps is a training program, not a job. Each center page shows only a few of its trades; use See More on the center page for the full list.

name: John Muir Health High School Student Volunteer Program (Walnut Creek Medical Center)
what_you_do: Help staff, patients and visitors at Walnut Creek Medical Center in a structured high school program. Students build skills in administration, patient interaction, communication, organization and leadership.
who_can_apply: Local high school students interested in a healthcare career. Must be at least 14.5 years old, at least a second-semester freshman, with a minimum 3.0 GPA. Must attend a Saturday orientation with a parent or guardian and complete required training. Students apply through a partner high school, which interviews and screens its own candidates.
pay_detail: Volunteer role; no pay stated on the page
duration: One 3-hour shift per week, year-round, committed through the end of senior year
deadline_text: No application window is stated on the official page. Contact a partner high school (for example Acalanes, Campolindo, Las Lomas, Miramonte, Monte Vista, San Ramon Valley or Ygnacio Valley) to ask about the next intake.
how_to_apply: Apply through your high school. Contact the career, college or community service office at a partner school listed on the page. The school interviews and screens its own student candidates.
notes: Read on the official John Muir Health page 2026-10-07. Not stated on that page: application window or deadline, TB test or immunization requirements. It is an unpaid volunteer role, so no work permit is listed. Region is east-bay because Walnut Creek is in Contra Costa County, not Oakland. The Auxiliary at Walnut Creek Medical Center offers selective scholarships to high school seniors and college students who volunteered in this program. A separate Concord Medical Center high school program is not onboarding this summer; its page says to check back in March 2027. An older third-party listing said seniors are not accepted, which conflicts with the official page; confirm with the program before applying. Minimum age is listed as 14.5 on the page, stored here as 14.

name: Junior Achievement of Northern California (high school programs)
what_you_do: You can join Junior Achievement programs on entrepreneurship, investing and personal finance, led by volunteers. Job shadow and Finance Park experiences are also listed, and a Silicon Valley Launchpad center is coming in early 2027.
who_can_apply: High school programs are delivered through schools and teachers, who request them. The site does not list a way for a student to sign up alone, so ask your school or call JA.
pay_detail: No student fee stated. JA says programs are little to no cost to educators.
duration: Varies
deadline_text: No central deadline; ask JA.
how_to_apply: Ask your teacher or counselor to request a JA program, or contact JA at (925) 465-1070 or info@janorcal.org.
notes: JA reached 27,947 students in 128 schools in 2025-26, mostly through schools. JA Launchpad (Silicon Valley) is listed as opening early 2027. Job shadow and internship details were not on the pages read, so ask JA.

name: KP LAUNCH High School Program
city: Northern California Kaiser Permanente service areas
what_you_do: You get a paid summer job. It is seven weeks and full time. The jobs are in healthcare support or admin roles. You also get weekly workshops, mentoring and networking. There is little patient contact.
grades: Current high school student (priority to juniors and seniors) or Class of 2027 graduate
who_can_apply: Be 16 to 19 by June 1, 2027, live in a Northern California Kaiser Permanente service area, have proof of legal US work eligibility, and be free Monday to Friday about 8am to 5pm. Priority goes to juniors and seniors. Children of Kaiser employees or physicians cannot apply. The program aims at students who lack resources to explore health careers.
pay_detail: $25 per hour minimum, paid every two weeks, up to 40 hours a week
duration: 7 weeks, June 14 to July 30, 2027
deadline_text: Opens Nov 16, 2026 at 9am Pacific; closes Jan 8, 2027 at 5pm Pacific.
how_to_apply: Apply only on the KP LAUNCH online portal during the window (email submissions are not reviewed). You need a resume and a personal statement of up to 750 words. Questions: KP.LAUNCH@kp.org.
notes: Full-time hours, so no summer school or camp overlap. Competitive. A Kaiser story reportedly cited about 3,300 applicants for 318 spots, which is not confirmed here. Placement sites vary, so check that your area is offered. Kaiser may ask for COVID vaccine proof.

name: Kane County Workforce Development Youth Services (WIOA Youth)
city: Kane, DeKalb and Kendall Counties (Elgin area), IL
what_you_do: You can get paid work experience. You can do internships and job shadowing. Apprenticeships are also an option. You get resume and interview coaching. You can get GED prep and tutoring. You also get help with life skills, transportation and child care.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24 who live in Kane, DeKalb or Kendall County. The page lists no income or other rules (federal workforce funding rules may apply, so ask the provider).
pay_detail: Paid work experience is one of the services; pay rate is not stated.
duration: Varies by provider
deadline_text: No dates posted. You contact a provider and they explain how to start.
how_to_apply: Pick a provider on the page and contact them directly. Providers in Kane County include Elgin Community College and Business & Career Services Inc. Waubonsee Community College covers Kane and Kendall. Not sure where to start? Call 630-762-2085.
notes: Starts at age 16, so it fits older high schoolers. The page names one contact person but lists an email that does not match that name, so phone first. Funded by a U.S. Department of Labor grant per the page. Elgin Community College's own Future Workforce Leaders program is one of the providers.

name: King County Library System Teen Advisory Boards
city: King County, WA (branches outside the city of Seattle)
what_you_do: Teen volunteers meet with a librarian. They give input on library services. They help design library programs and events.
who_can_apply: Teens. The page does not state ages; ask the teen librarian at your branch. Each board sets its own meeting schedule.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Members earn volunteer credit, and can ask for a reference letter after 10 hours of volunteering within 6 months.
duration: Ongoing; meeting schedules vary by branch
deadline_text: No deadline. The page lists upcoming meetings (for example Maple Valley, Lake Forest Park, Newport Way and Federal Way); contact the local library to join.
how_to_apply: Contact your local librarian (Teen Services Librarian). Or go to an open Teen Advisory Board meeting listed on the page. If your branch has no board, ask about starting one.
notes: KCLS serves King County outside the city of Seattle (its branches include Maple Valley, Lake Forest Park, Newport Way and Federal Way). The Seattle Public Library volunteer page showed no current volunteer openings when read on 2026-10-09. Washington L&I says its child labor rules 'only apply to minor employees, not volunteers.'

name: Key Club (high school service club)
what_you_do: You do service, leadership and fundraising through a student-led club at your school. If your school has no club, you can start one.
who_can_apply: Any high school student who wants to serve and lead. Clubs are set up in high schools or equivalent schools. Members are expected to do at least 50 hours of service a year.
pay_detail: No pay. Members pay nominal dues (amount not listed on the pages read).
deadline_text: Join your school's club or start one. No cycle stated.
how_to_apply: Use the Find a Key Club tool on keyclub.org, or follow the Start a Key Club steps if your school has none.
notes: Dues and local rules vary by club; dues amount not stated on the pages read. Key Club International phone: 800-549-2647.

name: Keystone Job Corps Center
org: U.S. Department of Labor Job Corps
what_you_do: Live on campus and train for a career at no cost. You also earn a high school diploma or equivalent. Training includes bricklayer, carpentry, cement masonry, plumbing and more.
who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules, or have other approved status. You must meet background rules. An Admissions Representative reads your application. This person decides if you can join.
pay_detail: Free to students. The campus page lists furnished dorms, meals, basic medical care, books and supplies, and a living allowance paid in cash twice a month.
duration: Not stated on the pages read
deadline_text: No deadline posted. You start by making a MyJobCorps account on the Job Corps website.
how_to_apply: Create a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Finish the application. Then an Admissions Representative sets up an interview. They review your documents and a background check. They also help you pick a campus.
notes: Mostly fits teens 16 and up who are out of school or want a different path. Housing: dorms are listed on the campus page. A center being listed on the Job Corps site does not prove it is enrolling right now, so confirm with an Admissions Representative. The training list above comes from the center's training page and may not be complete. Whether a state work permit applies was not checked.

name: Khan Academy college and careers courses
what_you_do: You can take free online lessons on the Khan Academy Life skills page. Topics include financial literacy, personal finance, entrepreneurship, career exploration and college admissions.
who_can_apply: Open to anyone. The site says its mission is a free education for anyone, anywhere. The page states no age rule.
pay_detail: Free (the site says it is a nonprofit offering free education)
duration: Self-paced
deadline_text: Always open.
how_to_apply: Go to the page, pick a course, and sign up for a free account if you want to save progress.
notes: The page loads slowly because it builds in your browser. Course list seen: Financial Literacy, Personal Finance, Entrepreneurship, Careers, College admissions, Career Exploration.

name: Kode With Klossy
city: Virtual and in-person (Oakland, San Francisco and more)
what_you_do: You can join a free coding program for girls and gender-expansive teens ages 13 to 18. Choices include a two-day Code-a-Bration or a two-week Camp in summer.
who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 18; no prior experience required for the free onboarding programs. Camps run in several cities including San Francisco and Oakland, plus virtual.
pay_detail: Free
duration: Code-a-Bration is 2 days; Camp is 2 weeks
deadline_text: Sign-ups are open for Code-a-Bration (Nov 7 to 8, 2026 in Oakland and virtual; Oct 17 to 18 in Chicago and virtual). Summer 2027 Camp applications open in February 2027; closing dates not posted.
how_to_apply: Use the sign-up form linked on the Kode With Klossy programs page.
notes: Free for all programs. Workforce development programs are for ages 18 to 26, not high schoolers. Camp dates and sites for summer 2027 are not posted yet.

name: LA County Library Teen Volunteer and Teen Advisory Board
org: County of Los Angeles Public Library
what_you_do: You can help at your local library. Tasks include kids' storytimes and art activities. You can help with computer and printing help. You can clean and sort materials and make displays. Teen Advisory Boards plan programs.
who_can_apply: Anyone 14 and older can volunteer. Teen Advisory Boards are open to teens at libraries that have one.
pay_detail: Unpaid; students can earn school service credit.
duration: Varies by library
deadline_text: No deadline. Ask your local LA County Library about current openings.
how_to_apply: Contact your local LA County Library branch to ask about volunteer openings and whether it has a Teen Advisory Board.
notes: This covers LA County Library branches (unincorporated areas and many cities), not the City of Los Angeles library system (see the LAPL card). Tasks vary by branch and season.

name: LA County Youth@Work
org: LA County Department of Economic Opportunity (DEO)
what_you_do: Do a paid, part-time first job with a local employer while taking a work-readiness class. You sign up through a nearby America's Job Center of California (AJCC).
who_can_apply: LA County residents who are 14 to 24 when they enroll and have the legal right to work in the U.S. The county gives priority to youth with high needs, such as current or former foster youth, youth touched by the justice system, youth who are or were homeless, and LGBTQ+ youth.
pay_detail: Paid work experience for about 140 hours plus a class. The page does not state an hourly wage.
