duration: About 160 hours in all: up to 140 hours of paid work plus 20 hours of job-readiness class
deadline_text: No deadline is posted. Fill out the youth interest form and an AJCC contacts you within 48 hours. In 2025 the summer jobs started July 1.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Youth Interest Form on the Youth@Work page. AJCC staff reach out within 48 hours to check eligibility and match you with an employer.
notes: The county released a Youth@Work Program Review and Redesign Report on August 25, 2026, so rules and pay for 2027 may change. Under 18 you need a California work permit before the first day. The pay figure is the 2025 summer rate from the county's own news release, not a 2027 promise. Long Beach youth can also use the City of Long Beach center (see the LBWIN card).

name: LACMA Teens
org: Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA)
what_you_do: You learn how museum education works. You plan and run an art workshop with other teens. LACMA staff guide you.
who_can_apply: Los Angeles County residents, 16 to 18, who will be juniors or seniors in the 2027 school year and are interested in art, museums or community events.
pay_detail: Selected teens receive a stipend. The amount is not stated.
duration: 10 sessions on select Sundays, 10 a.m. to 2:30 p.m., Oct 2026 to Feb 2027
deadline_text: 2026-27 cohort: applications ran July 1 to Aug 21, 2026 (5 p.m.) and are closed. The page says LACMA will not accept applications again until next year.
how_to_apply: Online application during the open window (last year July 1 to Aug 21). Questions go to teens@lacma.org.
notes: Next year's dates are not posted. Watch for a July opening. LACMA also offers NexGenLA, a free membership for LA County youth 17 and under (free museum entry plus one guest). Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.

name: Zoo Teens (ages 14-17)
org: Columbian Park Zoo, City of Lafayette Parks and Recreation
what_you_do: A structured summer volunteer program at the city zoo for teens curious about zookeeping, conservation and wildlife education. Builds customer service, time management and leadership skills.
who_can_apply: Teens who are 14 to 17 years old on June 1 of the year they apply. Teens interested in any career field may apply. A parent or guardian must co-sign the online application. A teacher or mentor recommendation form is part of the process.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program
duration: Summer; shift details are in the 2026 Zoo Teen Information Packet (not read)
deadline_text: 2026 application closed; materials were due March 13, 2026. The zoo page says to check back in January 2027.
how_to_apply: Read the Zoo Teen Information Packet, apply online through the zoo's volunteer form (applicant and parent both e-sign), and submit the teacher or mentor recommendation form. Contact: zooteen@lafayette.in.gov, 765-807-1543.
notes: Opening date for 2027 is not posted; the page only says check back in January 2027. The page mentions sponsors that keep costs low for participants but does not state a fee amount. The information packet was not read, so shift length and total hours are not stated here.

name: Food Finders Food Bank volunteer shifts
what_you_do: Sign up for volunteer shifts at the food bank. Family Night projects include bagging produce and assembling senior boxes. Teens 14 and older can also volunteer at the Fresh Market.
who_can_apply: Minimum age is 9. Everyone under 18 needs a waiver signed by a parent or guardian. Ages 9 to 15 need an adult chaperone (1 adult for every 5 youths). Individual 16 and 17 year olds can volunteer without a chaperone. Groups of 16 and 17 year olds need chaperones (1 adult for every 10 youths). You must be at least 14 to volunteer at the Fresh Market.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Training is given at the start of your first shift.
duration: Single shifts you pick on the calendar
deadline_text: No deadline. You can sign up for shifts up to 3 months ahead.
how_to_apply: Create a VolunteerHub account (a parent or guardian creates the profile for a child), pick a shift on the volunteer calendar, and bring the signed waiver to your first shift. Questions: call 765-471-0062.
notes: Some shifts have their own age rules. A parent or guardian needs to make the account for anyone under 18. Court ordered community service hours need separate approval before you start.

name: C-PASA High School Camp (Cargill-Purdue Agriculture & STEM Academy)
org: Purdue University College of Agriculture, Office of Academic Programs
what_you_do: Spend a week living on Purdue's campus. You do hands-on work in agriculture and STEM. You visit research sites and labs. You tour agriculture companies. You meet Purdue students and faculty. You see what college life is like.
who_can_apply: Students going into grades 9 to 12. No other rule is stated on the camp page.
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the camp page. Summer College for High School Students sets the price (see the Purdue Summer College card).
duration: 1 week, residential
deadline_text: The 2026 camp ran July 12 to 17, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted on the camp page.
how_to_apply: Apply through Purdue's Summer College for High School Students (the camp page says the 2026 application was there). Questions: purdueag@purdue.edu.
notes: This is a camp, not a job, and it costs money. The Purdue ag summer programs index page describes the high school camp as a two-week experience. The camp page itself says one week. Confirm the length with purdueag@purdue.edu.

name: Pulsar Summer Residential (Purdue GER2I, grades 9 to 12)
org: Purdue University Gifted Education Research and Resource Institute (GER2I)
what_you_do: Live in a Purdue residence hall for two weeks. You take challenging courses with other gifted and talented students. The program also includes field trips and recreation.
who_can_apply: Students entering grades 9 to 12 (the Pulsar level). New students send an essay or other media about their interest. They also send two of these. One is a transcript with a 3.5 GPA in the talent area. Others are a test score of 120 or higher on an intelligence test and a 90th percentile achievement or aptitude test. A teacher or mentor letter counts. So does proof of involvement such as awards.
pay_detail: 2026 listing: $2,990 per session for Star or Pulsar, plus a $100 application fee (refunded only if not accepted). Optional $100 Saturday field trip. A 5% early bird discount applied by Feb 17. A limited number of partial scholarships exist for students with financial need, first come, first served.
duration: 2 week sessions
deadline_text: 2026: registration opened Feb 2, 2026. Camp ran June 28 to July 25, 2026 in two sessions (June 28 to July 11, July 12 to 25). Payment was due June 1. 2027 dates are not posted.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application through the Purdue conferences site (the Register Now link on the program page). Upload your essay or media and two supporting documents. Questions: geri@purdue.edu or 765-494-7210.
notes: Costs money and is a camp, not a job. The details on this card came from a summarized fetch of the program page. The raw page would not load for a second check. Confirm the Pulsar price, dates and application steps with geri@purdue.edu or 765-494-7210 before you plan. The page also lists other prices ($1,250 commuter and $1,495 residential per session). They may be for the younger levels.

name: STEP: Seminar for Top Engineering Prospects (Purdue)
org: Purdue University College of Engineering Honors Program
what_you_do: Spend a week on Purdue's campus. You work in teams of four on engineering design challenges. There is a final design competition. You also tour two engineering areas. You learn about 3D modeling, programming and robotics.
who_can_apply: Rising high school seniors (Class of 2027 for the 2026 camp). Purdue recommends three years of high school math and one year of chemistry or physics by summer.
pay_detail: Attendance fee $2,500 for 2026. It covers activities, housing, meals and local transportation. You pay your own travel to Purdue. Need-based scholarships are available after you are accepted.
duration: 1 week, residential
deadline_text: 2026 sessions were July 5 to 11, July 12 to 18, July 19 to 25 and July 26 to Aug 1. Registration for 2026 has closed. 2027 dates are not posted.
how_to_apply: Apply online. A complete application needs your PSAT, SAT or ACT scores and a transcript. Applications are taken until spots are full, then a waiting list. Questions: step@purdue.edu or 765-494-7217.
notes: Costs money and is a camp, not a job. Only for students going into their senior year. The page gives 2026 information, so check it for the 2027 cycle.

name: Summer College for High School Students (short-term residential courses)
org: Purdue University, Office of Summer and Winter Sessions
what_you_do: You live on the West Lafayette campus for one or two weeks. You take a short college course. It is for 1 or 2 credit hours. Subjects include coding, cybersecurity, pharmacy, nursing, nuclear energy and business.
who_can_apply: High school students. Main page says ages 15 to 17. Application page: priority for GPA 3.30 or higher and at least 16 who have finished sophomore year, younger students may apply. Residential courses require being under 18 for the whole program. Course-specific rules apply.
pay_detail: Summer 2026 prices: $60 application fee. Tuition and fees $347.85 per credit hour for Indiana residents ($948.30 nonresident). Room and board $377.95 for a 1-week program, $907.08 for 2 weeks. Some courses add $60 or $200 program fees. Scholarships exist.
duration: 1 or 2 weeks, residential, June and July
deadline_text: Summer 2027 application opens December 1, 2026. Last cycle: priority deadline February 1, final deadline April 1. 2027 deadlines not posted.
how_to_apply: Online Summer College application: essay, high school transcript, up to three short-term course choices, $60 non-refundable fee. Admitted students first get one course; more are offered as space allows in late March to early April.
sources_fetched: https://www.purdue.edu/summer-high-school/What to Expect1/Applying to Summer College for High School Students.php
notes: Costs are summer 2026 and may change. Some courses were full for 2026 and some were canceled. The listed short courses include PREFACE and MITE, which are pre-college engineering workshops, with their own eligibility. The student pays; this is not a job.

name: Teen Volunteers, Summer Reading Club
what_you_do: Help run the library's Summer Reading Club: explain how it works, sign kids up, update the database and hand out prizes. One 2-hour shift a week.
who_can_apply: Teens who are 12 or older by May 31 of the program year. No grade rule is listed. The library's volunteer page is under its Teens section.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer
duration: Summer Reading Club season; at least one 2-hour shift per week
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: apply by Friday, May 22, 2026; required training day May 16 or May 23, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Google Form linked on the library's Teen Volunteers page, then attend one volunteer training day. Questions: Youth Department, 765-429-0119.
notes: The page was last updated for the 2026 season, so the next cycle should open in spring 2027 but is not posted yet. Check with the Youth Department before applying. Unpaid volunteering, so no Indiana work permit question applies.

name: Tippecanoe County 4-H
what_you_do: Join a 4-H club and do hands-on projects, including livestock and non-livestock projects. The county page also links to county fair entry and the Indiana State Fair.
grades: Grades 3 to 12 (Mini 4-H is grades K to 2)
who_can_apply: Youth in grades 3 to 12 can join a 4-H club in Indiana. Enroll through the Tippecanoe County Extension office.
pay_detail: $15 per child, $45 maximum per family. The fee covers insurance, project materials and club activities.
duration: Program year, enrollment starts Oct 1
deadline_text: Enrollment for the Indiana 4-H year begins October 1. The county page asks members to enroll by Jan 15 (and says Jan 1 to keep traditional involvement). The drop/add deadline for projects is May 15 each year.
how_to_apply: Create a family account and enroll each youth in 4HOnline 2.0 (links are on the county enrollment page). Call the Extension office at 765-474-0793 with questions.
notes: The county page gives two enrollment dates (Jan 15 and Jan 1), so ask the office which one applies. The Extension office is at 1950 South 18th Street, Lafayette, IN 47905. This is a youth club, not a paid job.

name: Teen Action Group (TAG) at East Lansing Public Library
org: East Lansing Public Library (City of East Lansing)
what_you_do: East Lansing High School students can log limited volunteer hours. They do this by joining our Teen Action Group.
who_can_apply: The library page says East Lansing High School students can log limited volunteer hours through the Teen Action Group. Ages are not stated.
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Not stated on the page.
deadline_text: No current dates found. The library is not currently accepting general volunteers; TAG is the exception named on the current page.
how_to_apply: For more information, contact Rheanna Reeder or Zandra Blake.
notes: The detailed TAG description is from a May 2022 library post that the site marks as possibly out of date, so confirm meeting times and who can join with the library first. Page also says the library is not accepting general volunteers at this time. Michigan's youth employment page (Youth Employment Standards Act) says the law covers employers of anyone under 18 including volunteers, so ask the program whether a work permit is needed.

name: PAN: Physics of Atomic Nuclei (FRIB, Michigan State University)
org: Facility for Rare Isotope Beams (FRIB), Michigan State University
what_you_do: Spend a week at a world-leading nuclear physics lab. You explore nuclear astrophysics research, run your own experiments, and learn how the science is used in society.
who_can_apply: Current high school students in the United States.
pay_detail: Free. The program, room and board are free for all participants.
duration: About 1 week, residential
deadline_text: The program takes place in late July each year. Applications are open early December through March. Exact 2027 dates are not posted on the page I could read.
how_to_apply: Apply through the program page linked from the MSU Spartan Youth listing. Contact: Zach Constan, constan@frib.msu.edu or 517-908-7363.
notes: The FRIB program page (frib.msu.edu) did not load for me because the site blocks automated readers, so this card rests on Michigan State University's Spartan Youth Programs listing only. Confirm dates, the application link, cost and any extra requirements on the FRIB page before you plan.

name: PING: Physicists Inspiring the Next Generation (FRIB, Michigan State University)
org: Facility for Rare Isotope Beams (FRIB), Michigan State University
what_you_do: Spend two weeks doing nuclear physics at the FRIB lab with undergraduate mentors. It can turn into a year-long research project. Students may present their work at national conferences.
who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12. The listing does not state other rules.
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the listing I could read.
duration: 2 weeks (2026: July 12 to 25)
deadline_text: The 2026 application deadline was March 15, 2026 and the program ran July 12 to 25, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted on the listing.
how_to_apply: Use the program page linked from the MSU Spartan Youth listing. Questions: ping@frib.msu.edu.
notes: The FRIB program page (frib.msu.edu) did not load for me because the site blocks automated readers. So this card rests on Michigan State University's Spartan Youth Programs listing only. Confirm dates, the application link, cost and any extra requirements on the FRIB page before you plan. Not a paid job.

name: Greater Lansing Food Bank Volunteer Shifts
what_you_do: You sort food and build Weekend Kits in the warehouse. Or you help at Mobile Food Pantries. In season, you can help with the Garden Project.
who_can_apply: All volunteers must be at least 14 years old.
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Single shifts; weekday warehouse shifts are about 2 hours
deadline_text: Sign up for open shifts any time; many shifts book 2 to 3 weeks out.
how_to_apply: Register once through Volunteer Hub, then pick a shift from the schedule. Groups of four or more email the volunteer program manager.
notes: Not teen-specific, but open to teens 14 and up. Warehouse shifts are 9 to 11 a.m. and 1:30 to 3:30 p.m. Monday to Friday, with some late afternoon, evening and weekend shifts at Mobile Food Pantries. Michigan's youth employment page (Youth Employment Standards Act) says the law covers employers of anyone under 18 including volunteers, so ask the program whether a work permit is needed.

name: Michigan 4-H Exploration Days (at Michigan State University)
org: Michigan State University Extension, Michigan 4-H Youth Development
what_you_do: Stay on the MSU campus with about 1,000 other youth and choose from more than 100 sessions taught by MSU faculty, staff and 4-H volunteers. You live in a dorm and eat in the dining hall.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 12 to 19 (the listing shows grades 6 to 12). The listing says to check with your county MSU Extension office about scholarship funds.
pay_detail: 2025 cost was $250. It covers meals, a shared dorm room, sessions and a t-shirt. Your county MSU Extension office may have scholarship money.
duration: 3 days (2026: June 24 to 26)
deadline_text: The 2026 event was June 24 to 26, 2026. 2027 dates and the 2026 price are not posted on the listing I could read.
how_to_apply: The listing links to a program page for details and registration, which I could not read. Contact on the listing: Michelle Neff, hydemich@msu.edu, 989-539-7805.
notes: The program's own 4-H page did not load for me. The Michigan State University College of Agriculture and Natural Resources site blocks automated readers. So this card rests on Michigan State University's Spartan Youth Programs listing only. Confirm dates, price and how to register on the 4-H page. It is a statewide event held in East Lansing, so it may also be listed as a Michigan-wide card. Not a job.

grades: Entering grades 10 to 12 in Fall 2027 (or recent graduates)
name: High School Engineering Institute (HSEI) at Michigan State University
org: Michigan State University College of Engineering
what_you_do: A week on campus living in the dorms. Each day you learn about an engineering major with faculty and students, do hands-on team projects and tour research labs.
who_can_apply: Co-ed. Open to U.S. and international students entering grades 10 to 12 in Fall 2027. You need a GPA of 3.0 or better in engineering core courses (math, sciences, technology). A transcript is required.
pay_detail: $1,199 program fee (covers activities, room and board). MSU says it offers no scholarships for its pre-college programs.
duration: One week, residential. Four sessions: June 13 to 17, June 20 to 24, June 27 to July 1, July 11 to 15
deadline_text: Applications open mid-December 2026. Deadlines by session: Session 1 June 4, Session 2 June 11, Session 3 June 18, Session 4 July 2. The page does not print the year; it is the cycle for students entering grades 10 to 12 in Fall 2027.
how_to_apply: Send an online application with your transcript. Payment by credit card is the last step. It is required before MSU reviews the application. If you are not accepted, the fee is refunded minus a $25 processing fee.
notes: Residential. Mentors supervise students in the dorms, and students cannot leave campus. Contact: future-engineer@egr.msu.edu or 517-353-7282 (from the college page). Check the year of the session dates against the application page when it opens.

grades: Entering grades 11 and 12 in Fall 2027 (or recent graduates)
name: Making a Game of It, AI Assisted (MGIT-AI) at Michigan State University
org: Michigan State University College of Engineering
what_you_do: This is a residential week. You learn to code and design. You build your own video games. You use AI as a coding and creative helper.
who_can_apply: Co-ed, open to U.S. and international students entering grades 11 and 12 in Fall 2027 with a GPA of 3.0 or better in engineering core courses. A transcript is required.
pay_detail: $1,299 program fee. MSU says it offers no scholarships for its pre-college programs.
duration: One week, residential: July 18 to 23
deadline_text: Applications open mid-December 2026. Application deadline: July 9. The page does not print the year; it is the cycle for students entering grades 11 and 12 in Fall 2027.
how_to_apply: Online application with transcript. Payment by credit card is the last step and is required before review. If not accepted, the fee is refunded minus a $25 processing fee.
notes: Residential with dorm supervision. Contact: future-engineer@egr.msu.edu or 517-353-7282. Check the year of the dates against the application page when it opens.

name: Zoo Teen Program at Potter Park Zoo
org: Potter Park Zoo (Potter Park Zoological Society and Ingham County)
what_you_do: You teach guests at conservation stations. You work with the goat contact yard. You help in the Zookambi summer camp. You learn about zoo careers from zookeepers.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 13 to 17 who can work independently, have reliable transportation to the zoo, and can work outside in all weather.
pay_detail: $50 program fee (shirt, training materials, name tag), paid at orientation, not at application. Scholarships are available.
duration: At least 40 hours of service from June to August
deadline_text: 2026 applications are closed. Information session dates and May 2027 orientation dates will be posted in January 2027. You must attend an information session to get the application.
how_to_apply: Step 1: attend an information session. Step 2: complete the application you receive afterward. Step 3: attend orientation and the required training. Keep a journal and finish monthly prompts.
notes: The zoo's volunteer page says teens 13 to 18 use this separate program; the program page itself says 13 to 17, so confirm the upper age. The regular adult volunteer program is 18 and older. Returning teens (years 3 to 5, under 18) can apply for the Zoo Teen Leadership Council. Contact is on the program page. Michigan's youth employment page (Youth Employment Standards Act) says the law covers employers of anyone under 18 including volunteers, so ask the program whether a work permit is needed.

grades: Entering junior year of high school or older (junior and senior students at local high schools)
name: UM Health-Sparrow Teen Volunteer Program
what_you_do: You can volunteer in one of six teen roles at the hospital. Examples are discharge, patient and visitor guide, bedside DJ and mother and baby. You work one short shift a week.
who_can_apply: Age 16 and entering junior year of high school. Some placements need volunteers to be 17, and the Radiology placement is for ages 17 to 18.
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: One semester (10 to 12 weeks): one 2 hour shift a week in the school year, or two shifts a week (max 4 hours) in summer
deadline_text: Volunteer applications are temporarily closed and are anticipated to reopen in mid-October.
how_to_apply: Online application on the Volunteering at Sparrow page (or ask for a paper copy at Volunteer Services). Then onboarding (2 to 3 weeks), online orientation, and placement registration links sent to onboarded volunteers.
notes: Expect a criminal background check, proof of MMR, varicella and Tdap immunizations (or titers), and a flu vaccine Nov to March; teens wear a provided smock apron and closed toe shoes. Volunteers must attend at least 75 percent of shifts. Free parking for active volunteers. Volunteer Services phone is on the page. Michigan's youth employment page (Youth Employment Standards Act) says the law covers employers of anyone under 18 including volunteers, so ask the program whether a work permit is needed.

name: Lao Family Community Development: Youth on the Move
what_you_do: You get a paid summer work experience of up to about 100 hours. You get job readiness training. It is through the City of Oakland's summer youth jobs program.
who_can_apply: Oakland youth ages 16 to 21, per the City of Oakland summer youth jobs partner table. You must live in Oakland for that program.
pay_detail: At least Oakland's minimum wage (MSYEP rule); exact rate not posted
duration: Up to about 100 hours
deadline_text: No dates posted. The Summer 2026 round is over; call for the next cycle.
how_to_apply: Call (510) 533-8850 or 1 (833) 532-3674, or use the Contact Us form at lfcd.org.
notes: LFCD's own employment page does not describe this youth program. Ages, hours and pay come from the City of Oakland MSYEP page. Under-18 workers need a work permit.

name: LAPL Teen Volunteer, Teen Council and Teens Leading Change
what_you_do: You volunteer at your branch library. You organize the teen area. You build displays. You help kids with homework. You help with summer reading. Teen Council and Teens Leading Change add a community project.
who_can_apply: Teen Volunteer and Teens Leading Change are for ages 14 to 19. Teen Council is for ages 11 to 19. Volunteers fill out a Teen Volunteer Intake Form and a parent or guardian signs a waiver.
pay_detail: Unpaid; you earn community service hours.
duration: Varies by branch; Teen Council members complete at least 20 community service hours
deadline_text: No deadline. Teens Leading Change projects form in September, but you can join anytime.
how_to_apply: Contact the Young Adult Librarian or Senior Librarian at your nearest library, then complete the intake form and parent waiver. Questions: Volunteer Engagement, 213-228-7490.
notes: LAPL hosts over 2,600 teen volunteers a year across 73 branches. Openings differ by branch. Some branches also have volunteer slots listed at volunteer.lapl.org.

name: Summer Youth Volunteer Program
org: Livermore Area Recreation and Park District (LARPD)
what_you_do: Teens help Livermore Area Recreation and Park District staff. They run summer camps, sports, arts and crafts. They run recreation programs. They can join open space projects with park rangers. Volunteers earn community service hours.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17. Volunteers under 18 need a parent or guardian to sign the Youth Volunteer Waiver. Students must attend a Summer Youth Volunteer orientation. Some roles have extra rules: Summer Nature Camp requires the Counselor in Training (CIT) program, and Open Space Jr. Docents require age 16 or older.
pay_detail: Volunteer position. Earn community service hours; no wage is listed.
duration: Summer weekly shifts. The 2026 FAQ says sign-ups start with a maximum of 2 weeks, with more weeks added later.
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: sign up for orientation by Friday, March 13, 2026. Orientations were March 19, 2026 (5 to 6:30 pm) and March 25, 2026 (4 to 5:30 pm) at the Robert Livermore Community Center. 2027 dates are not posted yet.
how_to_apply: Create a LARPD volunteer account by submitting the General Volunteer Application (use a personal email, not a school email). Attend a Summer Youth Volunteer orientation at the Robert Livermore Community Center. Then sign up for shifts through MyImpactPage. Questions: volunteer@larpd.org.
notes: The 2026 cycle is closed. Watch larpd.org/volunteer and the orientation pages for the 2027 dates; the district's pages were not all updated to the same year. The FAQ says the opportunity list may change each year. The orientation and FAQ pages list volunteer@larpd.org as the contact. Not a paid job, so no California work permit is needed.

name: Las Positas College CCAP Dual Enrollment
what_you_do: You can take free Las Positas College classes in high school. The classes focus on career technical pathways. Partner programs are in Dublin, Livermore, Pleasanton and Tri-Valley. Tuition and fees are waived. Required materials are provided.
who_can_apply: High school students in partner districts: Dublin, Livermore, Pleasanton and Tri-Valley, plus San Ramon Valley USD (welding) and TUSD (fire safety training). Residency and citizenship rules apply; ask Admissions & Records.
pay_detail: Free; tuition and fees waived and required materials provided (parking may cost extra for classes at LPC)
duration: Per term
deadline_text: Rolling by term.
how_to_apply: Sign the CCAP Dual Enrollment form with your school counselor. You sign it once for all of high school. Questions: lpc-dualenrollment@laspositascollege.edu.
notes: Offered during and after the school day. Ages are not stated on the page.

name: Berkeley Lab Director's Apprenticeship Program (BLDAP)
what_you_do: You spend six weeks in person at Berkeley Lab, at least 4 days a week. You work on machine learning and data science projects, take computer science classes and hear talks from scientists.
who_can_apply: Grades 10 and 11. Public school students in Alameda, San Francisco and Contra Costa counties are prioritized; nearby counties are encouraged to apply. In person at Berkeley Lab at least 4 days a week for 6 weeks.
pay_detail: Not stated on the page (no stipend listed)
duration: June 16 to July 24, 2026 (6 weeks, 4 days a week)
deadline_text: 2026 applications opened Feb 2, 2026 and are now closed (the page gives no closing date). 2027 not posted.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the Berkeley Lab K-12 program page when it opens (the 2026 application ran through apply.mykaleidoscope.com).
notes: Whether students are paid is not stated. Finishing students can join later workshops and possible lab internships in following summers.

name: Experiences in Research
what_you_do: You get a paid six-week summer research internship with a Berkeley Lab mentor. Areas include data science, experimental research, coding and science communication.
who_can_apply: Grades 10 to 12 in Northern California, at least 16 by the program start. Students within 30 miles of the lab are prioritized. You can do the program only once.
pay_detail: $500 per week for 30 to 35 hours
duration: 6 weeks (June 15 to July 24 in 2026)
deadline_text: 2026 window was Feb 2 to Mar 22, 2026. 2027 not posted.
how_to_apply: Apply online during the window and pick your top three projects. Do not contact mentors directly. Oakland Unified students also fill out a supplemental application.
notes: The page still says 'at least 16 by June 16, 2025', so check the age date when it reopens. Some 2026 projects were hybrid or virtual. Under-18 interns need a work permit.

name: SeA Bilingual STEM Camp
what_you_do: This is a free spring break camp at Berkeley Lab. It is for bilingual students. They are native Spanish speakers and English learners. It shows students careers in science, technology, engineering and math.
who_can_apply: English-learning, native Spanish-speaking bilingual students.
pay_detail: Free
duration: April 8 to 11, 2026 (spring break)
deadline_text: 2026 applications are closed; no 2027 dates posted.
how_to_apply: Watch the Berkeley Lab K-12 high school programs page.
notes: Grades and ages are not listed on the page. The 2026 camp is over and no 2027 camp is posted, so it is not confirmed to repeat. Page says it can lead to summer internship chances.

name: LBWIN Youth Career Services Center
org: City of Long Beach Economic Development and Opportunity, Workforce Development Bureau
what_you_do: You can get free career help at a youth center. Services include work-readiness workshops and help finding jobs. You can get paid internships or work experience such as Youth@Work.
who_can_apply: The center serves ages 14 to 30. Youth@Work is for ages 14 to 24 and WIOA Youth services are listed for ages 16 to 24. WIOA funding focuses on out-of-school youth with barriers such as low income, foster care, homelessness, juvenile justice involvement, parenting, or a disability. A Long Beach residency rule is not stated on the page.
pay_detail: Paid internships and Youth@Work (about 160 hours of paid work experience). Pay rates are not stated. Workshops and career help are free.
duration: Varies by program
deadline_text: No deadline is posted. The competitive school-to-career programs (Long Beach Public Service Corps, Port of Long Beach internship, Fire Corps internship and others) open for set application periods.
how_to_apply: Complete the Youth Interest Form on the city's Youth Services page. Partner agencies can also refer youth through the Unite Us platform.
notes: Because most WIOA funding targets youth facing barriers, a teen still in school may be steered to Youth@Work or a school-to-career program instead. Under 18 you need a California work permit for any paid placement. The city's Youth Opportunities page also lists teen volunteering at Long Beach libraries and at Parks, Recreation and Marine (ages 13 and up).

name: League of Volunteers Teen Volunteers (Summer Recreation)
city: Newark, CA (serves Fremont, Newark and Union City)
what_you_do: You help lead activities. You assist staff at the League's summer recreation program for kids. The League says teen volunteers gain leadership experience.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17. The page does not state a residency rule for volunteers.
duration: The 2026 summer recreation program ran July 6 to July 30, 2026, Monday to Thursday, 10 a.m. to 2 p.m., at Mayhews Landing Park in Newark.
deadline_text: The homepage showed a 2026 summer teen volunteer call. No 2027 dates are posted.
how_to_apply: Use the Register to Volunteer link for the teen volunteer call on the League site, or email lov@lov.org. Phone (510) 793-5683.
notes: The teen call on the homepage is for summer 2026. Confirm with the League whether it recruits again for 2027. Serves the Tri-Cities (Fremont, Newark and Union City).

name: LegiSchool Civics Virtual Institute
org: Sacramento State Center for California Studies with the California State Legislature
what_you_do: You can take a four-week online summer program about California policy. It includes talks from state leaders. It also includes professional skills workshops. You earn a stipend at the end.
who_can_apply: California high school sophomores, juniors and seniors. A select number are chosen.
pay_detail: Stipend paid after the program. The amount is not posted.
duration: 4 weeks, Mon/Wed/Fri afternoons (2026: starts June 22)
deadline_text: 2026 applications closed May 31, 2026. 2027 dates not posted yet.
how_to_apply: Apply through the LegiSchool website application. Join their mailing list for contest, town hall and internship news.
notes: The application link and 2027 dates are not on the page. The stipend amount is not stated. LegiSchool also runs Town Hall meetings in downtown Sacramento. It also runs video and essay contests for California high school students.

name: Teen Internship (Summer Camp Staff)
org: Lawrence Hall of Science, UC Berkeley
what_you_do: You help run science summer camps by leading games and activities, preparing materials and supporting campers. Training is in May, and the job is full time in summer.
who_can_apply: Students entering 11th or 12th grade. You must be able to work full time all summer. You must go to May Saturday trainings.
pay_detail: $3,500 for the full summer ($72 deducted per missed day)
duration: June 1 to Aug 7, 2026, Monday to Friday 8:30 am to 4:30 pm; Saturday trainings in May
deadline_text: 2026 applications closed January 15, 2026. Expect a similar mid-January deadline for 2027.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Lawrence Hall of Science teen internship page when it reopens; questions to lhscamps@berkeley.edu.
notes: The page URL says 2024 but the content is the 2026 posting. The page says to apply next summer; 2027 dates are not posted. Mid-January is the 2026 pattern only.

name: Lawrence Hall of Science Youth Volunteers
org: Lawrence Hall of Science, UC Berkeley
what_you_do: You staff exhibits such as the planetarium. Others are Ingenuity Challenges, Outdoor Nature Lab and Animal Discovery Zone. The minimum is 21 summer hours. During the school year, it is 2 shifts a month.
who_can_apply: Entering 9th grade or older and age 14 by June 1 (2024 cycle wording); not a current volunteer. Own transportation to Berkeley.
duration: Summer minimum 21 hours; school year two 3-hour shifts a month
deadline_text: Paused: no new cohort in 2025, with a relaunch planned for 2026 (page text dates from Dec 2024). Last posted window closed Jan 16, 2024. No current cohort confirmed.
how_to_apply: Check the Lawrence Hall of Science teen volunteer page; contact veronicau@berkeley.edu or 510-642-5132.
notes: The volunteer page now says it is not taking new adult volunteers and lists no teen program. Call or email to ask whether the redesigned teen program has launched. The age rules in who_can_apply come from 2024 wording, so the age fields are blank.

name: Livermore Area Youth Advisory Commission (LAYAC)
what_you_do: Youth members advise the City Council and the Livermore recreation district on what young people need. They also organize events that promote respect for diversity among Livermore youth.
who_can_apply: Youths ages 12 through 20, preferably attending Livermore schools. Youth members who attend Livermore schools do not have to live in the city (Livermore Municipal Code 2.51.010).
pay_detail: Advisory commission seat. No pay is stated in the code.
deadline_text: Application dates not found. The city teen page that would list them returned an access block to our reads.
how_to_apply: Not confirmed. Contact the City of Livermore to ask how to apply and when the next seats open.
notes: Confirm first. The membership and duties come from Livermore Municipal Code Chapter 2.51, read on the code publisher's page. The city's own teen page (livermoreca.gov) returned HTTP 403 to both our fetch tools, so the application process, term, and dates are not confirmed. The municipal code gives 15 youth seats and 3 adult seats; the code does not say how seats are filled. Re-checked on 2026-10-09: the City teen page returned HTTP 403 again, so it could not be read and the card stays snippet-only.

name: Discovery Program (Summer Health Sciences)
what_you_do: This is a two-week summer program on the Loma Linda campus. It is for high school students interested in health sciences careers.
who_can_apply: High school students in 9th through 12th grade in the Inland Empire who are interested in health sciences. Students 17 and a half or older may be invited to an optional shadowing week.
pay_detail: $30 non-refundable application fee (fee waiver available for financial need). The page does not list a program cost.
duration: 2 weeks (2026: July 12 to July 24), plus optional shadowing week
deadline_text: 2026 applications ran Jan 12 to April 12, 2026. 2027 dates not posted; expect a similar January to April window.
how_to_apply: Submit the application form, a recommendation form from a teacher or clergy member, a 200-word essay on your interest in health sciences, and the $30 fee or a waiver request.
notes: Closed until the next cycle opens. Loma Linda University is a Seventh-day Adventist institution.

name: Teen Docent Program, Los Altos History Museum
what_you_do: Teen docents work with museum staff, lead tours of the exhibits and the J. Gilbert Smith House, greet visitors and help at special events. They also take on leadership roles.
grades: High school student enrolled in the 2026-27 academic year
who_can_apply: High school students enrolled in the 2026-27 academic year.
pay_detail: Not stated on the current page. A 2024 article describes volunteer hours and work experience.
duration: August 2026 through June 2027, at least 4 hours per month. Two-day training on August 8 and 9 for accepted applicants.
deadline_text: Applications for 2026-27 are closed (the page says the deadline for this year has passed). The museum says to check back next spring for the 2027-28 year.
how_to_apply: Online Teen Docent Program application, linked from the museum site (closed for 2026-27). A 2024 article says selected applicants are called in for a brief interview.
notes: Phone 650.948.9427; the page gives no email address. Pay is not stated on the current official page, so we list it as unpaid based on a 2024 article; confirm with the museum. The lahstalon.org article is a 2024 news piece, used only for the interview and volunteer details. The museum's adult docent roles are separate and not for teens.

name: Los Rios Dual Enrollment and CCAP (American River, Cosumnes River, Folsom Lake, Sacramento City)
what_you_do: You can take free college classes while in high school. You can enroll on your own at a Los Rios college (special admit), or take a college class at your high school through an agreement between your school and the college.
who_can_apply: At least 14 years old or already started ninth grade. Needs a parent or guardian signature and a recommendation from your high school principal.
pay_detail: Tuition is free. Other fees may apply, such as the student representation fee. Books may cost extra.
duration: Per semester
deadline_text: No single deadline. Apply and register by each college's term dates.
how_to_apply: Talk to your high school counselor, pick the Los Rios college that offers the class, apply at that college as a dual enrollment student (parent signature and principal recommendation needed), then register.
notes: Credits go on a permanent college transcript. Whether you also get high school credit depends on your school, so ask your counselor. Your school does not need a CCAP agreement for you to take a college class. Application deadlines are by college term.

name: Madison Children's Museum Volunteers
what_you_do: You help kids play and learn at the museum. You can help with Rooftop Ramble animals and gardens. You can help in Art Studio or be a Play Ambassador. You can help in the outdoor Wonderground from April to October.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 and up can volunteer on their own. Ages 8 to 13 can volunteer with a caregiver.
pay_detail: Unpaid.
duration: One 2-hour shift each week for at least two months
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Shifts are filled first come, first served.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer application form on the page, clear a background check, interview (in person, Zoom or phone), attend orientation, then sign up for shifts on Sign Up Genius.
notes: Volunteer Coordinator: Tim Gruber, tgruber@madisonchildrensmuseum.org. Spots may be limited at any given time, so email before you apply.

name: TEENworks at Goodman Community Center
what_you_do: These are paid teen jobs at the community center, with training. All teens earn ServSafe certification and get event catering training. They can also earn high school credit.
who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12 (the page says the high school programs serve grades 9-12). Other rules are not stated.
pay_detail: Hourly wage; the rate is not stated.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No dates or enrollment status are posted on the page.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the page. Contact the program: TEENworks Manager Trevor Moores or High School Manager Vernon Hill (608-204-8039), or the center at 608-241-1574, info@goodmancenter.org.
notes: Confirm pay, hours and whether enrollment is open by phone. If you are 14 or 15, Wisconsin generally requires a work permit for paid work (see the Wisconsin rules on this site). Address: 214 Waubesa St, Madison.

name: Zoo Teen Program
what_you_do: This is an eight-week summer program on conservation. You go behind the scenes at the zoo. You hear from local conservation groups. You work with animal care and environmental professionals.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17 at the start of the program. Residency is not stated. Teens need reliable transportation to and from the zoo.
pay_detail: $200 per teen for the summer. Scholarships are available. Applying is free and payment is due only after you are invited.
duration: 8 weeks, two days a week (June 22 to Aug 21 in 2026)
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: applications opened Jan 28 and closed Mar 1, 2026; notified Mar 2 to 13. 2027 dates not posted yet.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application form (Google Form linked on the program page). Optional Zoom info sessions were held in February. Questions: education@henryvilaszoo.gov.
notes: The page still shows the Summer 2026 schedule, so the 2027 dates are a guess based on last year. The page's email link points to volunteer@henryvilaszoo.gov while the text says education@henryvilaszoo.gov, so check both. Phone on the page: 608-266-4732. Not a paid job.

name: Henry Vilas Zoo Volunteer Program (teens 14 to 17)
what_you_do: Help at the zoo in roles such as gate greeter, goat yard attendant, events and wildlife champion. Training is given.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17 can volunteer on their own in many roles. Ages 10 to 14 can volunteer with a parent or guardian in some roles (gate greeters, goat yard, events, wildlife champions).
pay_detail: Unpaid. The zoo does not do last-minute school hour confirmations.
duration: Seasonal; commitment varies by role
deadline_text: Applications for ongoing roles are posted each year between February and April.
how_to_apply: Pick a role on the zoo's Volunteer Roles page and fill out the application at the bottom of that role's page. Join the volunteer email list through the Volunteer Inquiry Form to hear about openings and information sessions.
notes: If you need school-required hours, check with your school counselor first. The zoo does not currently support court-ordered community service hours.

name: MMoCA Teen Forum
what_you_do: Learn how an art exhibition is made. Create and run educational programs. Meet museum and arts professionals through job shadows.
who_can_apply: 11th and 12th grade students from the Madison area who care about the arts.
pay_detail: Members are paid a stipend. The amount is not stated.
duration: 6 to 8 hours per month, in person at MMoCA, through the year
deadline_text: The page says applications were closed for the 2025 Teen Forum. No 2026-27 dates are posted.
how_to_apply: Not described on the page. Call MMoCA at (608) 257-0158 to ask when the next application opens.
notes: The page may be out of date (it mentions the 2025 group), so confirm by phone before planning around it. Small group.

name: Operation Fresh Start Legacy Program
what_you_do: You do paid, hands-on conservation or construction work. You get mentoring while you work toward a diploma. You earn an AmeriCorps Education Award when you finish.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24 in the Dane County area. Juniors and seniors need a referral from their home school. MMSD applicants must be entering the fourth quarter of junior year before applying.
pay_detail: Bi-weekly stipend (amount not stated). Finishers may earn an AmeriCorps Education Award of about $2,800 for college.
duration: At least 1,000 program hours (total length not stated)
deadline_text: No deadline listed. The page says Legacy is accepting applications.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now button on the Legacy page (opens a Google Form). Seniors and juniors also need a referral from their home school.
notes: Free program. Staff mentor graduates for one year after completion. Phone (608) 244-4721, info@operationfreshstart.org, 2670 Milwaukee St, Madison. The program starts at 16, so the Wisconsin permit rule for 14 and 15 year olds does not apply to it.

name: Madison Public Library Volunteering (teens welcome)
what_you_do: Help a library branch with tasks. Tasks include pulling books for holds and packing maker kits. You can package seeds for the Seed Library. You can set up for programs.
who_can_apply: The form has an age category of '17 and under', and the page says teens can volunteer to complete school hours. A minimum age is not stated.
pay_detail: Unpaid.
duration: Varies by branch
deadline_text: No deadline. Openings change by branch and season; several branches had no openings on the day the page was read.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer form (area of interest, availability, branch). Staff reply by email. A background check is required under City of Madison APM 2-44.
notes: On Oct 9, 2026 the page said Central Library had no openings and asked high school students needing hours (for example National Honor Society) to check back in fall 2026. Alicia Ashman, Hawthorne, Lakeview and Meadowridge listed no openings or a waitlist. Ask a branch before counting on hours.

name: Accelerated Learning Program (Badger Precollege)
what_you_do: Three weeks on the UW-Madison campus focused on one college-level course (95 class hours).
who_can_apply: Students finishing grades 9 to 12 from Wisconsin, across the U.S. and abroad. Admission usually looks at advanced coursework, a 3.2 unweighted GPA or similar, and essays. No age range is stated.
pay_detail: 2026: domestic residential $4,750; commuter $2,850; international $5,100; plus a $100 application fee (fee waivers can be requested). Scholarships exist (see notes).
duration: 3 weeks (June 28 to July 17 in 2026)
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: applications opened Jan 12, scholarships due Apr 1, application deadline May 1, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.
how_to_apply: Online application with two essays (about 500 words total) and an unofficial transcript.
notes: Full scholarship for Wisconsin residents who get free or reduced lunch; partial scholarship (up to 50%) with income paperwork; none for international students. Funds are limited. Contact info@precollege.wisc.edu or 608-890-3260.

name: Badger Summer Scholars (Badger Precollege)
what_you_do: Take a college-level course of your choice for two weeks on the UW-Madison campus. Residential students live in a residence hall.
who_can_apply: Students finishing grades 9 to 12. Admission usually looks at a 3.0 unweighted GPA or similar, coursework, interest in the course and essays. No age range is stated.
pay_detail: 2026: domestic residential $4,450; commuter $2,600; international $4,800; plus a $100 application fee (fee waivers can be requested). Scholarships exist (see notes).
duration: About 2 weeks (July 19 to 31 in 2026)
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: applications opened Jan 12, scholarships due Apr 1, application deadline May 1, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.
how_to_apply: Online application with two short essays (about 500 words total) and an unofficial transcript. Decisions come on the 2nd and 4th Monday of each month.
notes: Full scholarship for Wisconsin residents who get free or reduced lunch; partial scholarship (up to 50%) with income paperwork; none for international students. Funds are limited and first come, first served. Contact info@precollege.wisc.edu or 608-890-3260.

grades: Current sophomore or junior (the page also says 'rising juniors and seniors', so confirm)
name: Engineering Summer Program (ESP)
what_you_do: This is a three-week program on campus. You study math, physics, chemistry and engineering design. You do hands-on workshops. You visit industry sites. Faculty mentor you.
who_can_apply: U.S. citizens or permanent residents. Need at least a year each of algebra and geometry, a 3.0 unweighted GPA and a strong interest in math, science and engineering. Highly selective.
pay_detail: Free: housing and meals included. No stipend is mentioned.
duration: 3 weeks (July 11 to 31 in 2026), residential
deadline_text: 2026 application is closed and decisions were sent. No 2027 deadline posted.
how_to_apply: Online application, a high school transcript and a recommendation form. Questions: esp@engr.wisc.edu.
notes: Students live in Dejope Hall with supervision from staff and undergraduate counselors. Laundry and vending cost extra.

name: UW Health Teen Volunteer Program
what_you_do: You volunteer in a UW Health hospital or clinic. You do it for a full semester. You need a placement interview and onboarding first.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 16 and up who can commit to at least one full semester.
pay_detail: Unpaid.
duration: At least one full semester
deadline_text: Application closed now. Spring semester applications are expected to open Dec 2, 2026, with onboarding finished by Jan 8, 2027. Summer expected to open Apr 12, 2027; fall expected in July 2027. All dates are subject to change.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Wisconsin volunteer application on the UW Health volunteer page when it opens. Onboarding takes several weeks: online trainings, health assessment, placement interview, caregiver background check.
notes: Health clearance is required: seasonal flu shot, MMR, varicella, Tdap and a TB blood test. The page says waivers and exemptions are not accepted. Volunteer Services: (608) 263-6046, volunteer.services@uwhealth.org. The same page also covers Illinois locations; this card is for the Wisconsin application.

name: WIOA Youth Program (WorkSmart Network)
org: Workforce Development Board of South Central Wisconsin
what_you_do: This is free career planning, skills training and work-based learning. A career planner builds a plan with you.
who_can_apply: Young adults ages 16 to 24 in south central Wisconsin (job centers in Dane, Sauk and Jefferson counties). Whether in-school youth qualify is not stated.
pay_detail: Free. The page says all WorkSmart Network services are free of charge and does not say anyone is paid.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No deadline. The page says the online application is coming soon.
how_to_apply: Go to a free info session. It is listed on Eventbrite from the page. Or visit a Job Center, or call 608-249-9001.
notes: Eligibility rules (such as income) are not on the page, so call before you count on a paid placement.

name: Wisconsin Youth Apprenticeship (Dane and Jefferson counties)
org: Workforce Development Board of South Central Wisconsin
what_you_do: Spend part of the week in class and part on a paid job with a business mentor. There are 16 program areas. It lasts 1 or 2 years.
who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors in participating Dane and Jefferson county school districts. Employers choose and hire apprentices.
pay_detail: Paid while working; wage not stated.
duration: 1 or 2 years
deadline_text: No application deadline listed. Virtual information nights (7:00 to 7:45 pm): Nov 18, 2026; Dec 16, 2026; Jan 20, 2027; Mar 17, 2027; and Feb 17, 2027 (UW Health sessions).
how_to_apply: Contact your school district's School to Career Coordinator (the page lists a name and phone for each district, for example Madison Metropolitan: Annie Johnston, 608-663-5384). Register for an information night on the program page.
notes: One date on the page is shown as Jan 20, 2027 even though its registration link says 2026, so check it. Students interested in UW Health need the Feb 17 session. Main office 608-249-9001. Ask the coordinator whether your age needs a Wisconsin work permit.

name: Major League Hacking (MLH) hackathons
what_you_do: Major League Hacking runs student hackathons. These are short coding contests. It also runs coding events. It has a 12-week remote Fellowship that pays a stipend. Most listed hackathons do not say high school students can enter.
who_can_apply: Rules differ by event. On the 2027 events list only one event (hackPHS in New Jersey) is marked High School. The Fellowship page gives no age or student rule. Read each event page.
pay_detail: Event costs are not listed on the pages read; check each event. The Fellowship pays a stipend (amount not stated).
duration: Weekend events; Fellowship is 12 weeks
deadline_text: Dates differ by event. See the 2027 season events list. California events listed: DiamondHacks (La Jolla, Apr 4 to 5, 2027) and LA Hacks (Los Angeles, Apr 16 to 18, 2027).
how_to_apply: Browse the events list on mlh.com and read each event's age rule before registering.
notes: The pages read did not state a minimum age. Many MLH events are aimed at college students, so check before you plan travel.

name: The Maryland Zoo Teen Volunteer Program
what_you_do: Start as a Zoo Guide answering visitor questions, then choose a track such as guest engagement or conservation and research. Teens get training from zoo staff, a uniform and a badge.
who_can_apply: High school students ages 14 to 17. You must be 14 or older by Teen Boot Camp.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering. The page mentions no fees.
duration: At least one year: 4 shifts a month, one shift at a zoo event, and a one-week Boot Camp (Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.)
deadline_text: Teen applications are closed. The page says to check back in 2027. For 2026, applications ran Jan 29 to Apr 9, interviews were in May, and Boot Camp ran in late June and early July.
how_to_apply: Turn in the full application when it opens. Incomplete ones are not considered. Then go to a group interview. Questions: volunteers@marylandzoo.org or 443-552-5266.
notes: 2026 timeline from the page: selections May 28, parent orientation June 10, Boot Camp sessions June 22 to 26 and June 29 to July 3. The page text is partly inconsistent about dates, so check it when it updates. The Teens menu also lists a Keeper-in-Training Camp that was not read.

name: Massachusetts 4-H
what_you_do: Join a 4-H club or a short-term 4-H program at a library or community center. Pick your own projects, build skills and enter competitions if you are 8 or older.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 8 to 18 (before January 1) can join and take part in projects and competitions. Ages 5 to 7 join as Cloverbuds and do not compete.
pay_detail: $40 per member each year, with a family cap of $120. Fee waivers can be requested through your 4-H Educator. The page says cash is not accepted.
duration: Annual membership; you re-enroll each year
deadline_text: No deadline posted. All members enroll every year.
how_to_apply: Contact your local 4-H office to learn about programs and get the New Member Enrollment Packet. Fill it out and return it. The office then tells your parent or guardian where to pay online or by check. Re-enroll through 4honline.
notes: A youth group, not a job. The Get Involved page still shows a 2022-2023 fee note, but the Membership page lists the $40 fee with a $120 family cap, so confirm the current fee with your local office.

name: Massachusetts Girls State
org: American Legion Auxiliary, Department of Massachusetts
city: Massachusetts (2026 session at Stonehill College, Easton)
what_you_do: Spend a week running a pretend city and state. You campaign, write and debate bills, and learn how local and state government work.
grades: Finishing or just finished junior year of high school
who_can_apply: Girls who are finishing or just finished their junior year. You must be a U.S. citizen or legal inhabitant. Documents are needed at check-in. You need an interest in government, strong leadership and above average grades. A sponsor is needed.
pay_detail: No pay. Participants are sponsored by an American Legion post, Auxiliary unit, school or community group. The student cost is not stated on the pages read.
duration: One week (2026: June 13 to June 19)
deadline_text: The 2026 session was June 13 to June 19, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.
how_to_apply: Find a sponsor (a Legion post, Auxiliary unit, school or other group). Once your sponsor sends your name and email, the site emails you the online registration form. If you have no sponsor, fill out the sponsor request form on the Registration Forms page.
notes: Girls only. You can also send in an optional bill to be considered by the mock state Congress. The program says it is run by volunteers. Email Director.massgirlsstate@gmail.com with questions.

name: Massachusetts Boys State
org: The American Legion, Massachusetts Boys State Committee
what_you_do: Spend a week at Stonehill College running a pretend state government. You take classes, run for office, join a band, court or newspaper, and play sports.
grades: Finished 11th grade, with at least one semester of high school left
who_can_apply: Boys who finished junior year and have at least one semester left. You cannot have gone to a Boys State before. Leadership, character, grades and service to your school are what count. A parent and a family doctor must sign a medical consent form.
pay_detail: No pay. The goal is that tuition is paid by your local American Legion post, the Massachusetts Boys State and Girls State Foundation, a school or town, or a sponsor.
duration: One week: the 83rd Annual Session is June 12 to June 18, 2027
deadline_text: Session dates: June 12 to June 18, 2027. The site says applications open in late 2026. No closing date is posted.
how_to_apply: Fill out the program interest form on the site. You will be told when applications open (late 2026). The application has your information and a short response on what Boys State would mean to you. It also has a reference from a teacher or guidance counselor. You can also ask your local Legion post or guidance counselor.
notes: Boys only (Massachusetts Girls State is a separate program). You are expected to attend the whole week. It falls during many schools' finals, so ask your school about make-up plans early. The interest form link is the one on the home page.

name: Civil Air Patrol Cadet Program, Massachusetts Wing
what_you_do: Join a local squadron for weekly meetings. Learn leadership, aerospace, fitness and character. Wear a uniform. Move up in rank as you take on more leadership.
who_can_apply: Be at least 12 and not yet 19. Be a U.S. citizen or a lawful permanent resident (National Headquarters can waive this for some lawfully admitted noncitizens). Attend at least three squadron meetings.
pay_detail: Annual dues of $25 to $50 depending on location. Uniform and overnight activity fees are extra. National Headquarters says a fully active cadet may spend $300 to $600 in the first year. Some help is available.
duration: Ongoing. Weekly 2-hour meetings, about one Saturday event a month and a week-long summer encampment (typical, per national page)
deadline_text: No deadline. Join any time by visiting a squadron.
how_to_apply: Find a squadron with the unit locator. Visit a meeting with your parents. Go to at least three weekly meetings. Then fill out the application. You can also ask the squadron about the online application.
notes: No military duty. Cadets can stay in until age 21 and can switch to adult membership at 18. Squadron meetings and costs vary, so ask the squadron near you.

name: Massachusetts FFA
what_you_do: Join an FFA chapter at a school that teaches agricultural education. FFA builds leadership, personal growth and career skills. It does this through hands-on experiences.
who_can_apply: Students at a Massachusetts school with an FFA chapter. The state site lists the chapters (the list includes vocational, technical and agricultural high schools). It does not state an age rule.
pay_detail: Costs are not stated on the pages read. Ask your ag teacher.
duration: Ongoing while you are in agricultural education
deadline_text: No deadline posted. You join through your school.
how_to_apply: Find your school on the Massachusetts FFA Chapters page. The page does not say how to join, so ask your school how to sign up.
notes: The chapters page lists schools such as Bay Path Regional Vocational Technical H.S. in Charlton, Bristol County Agricultural High School in Dighton and Minuteman High School. Check the full list for your area. The site describes FFA as an intracurricular student group.

name: UMass Amherst Pre-College Summer Programs
org: University of Massachusetts Amherst, University Without Walls
city: Amherst, MA (also online and the UMass Charles River Campus in Boston)
what_you_do: Take a faculty-led summer course for high school students in over 25 topics like STEM, art and design, and business. A six-week lab research option is also offered.
grades: Rising sophomores, juniors and seniors (some programs only juniors and seniors)
who_can_apply: Rising sophomores, juniors and seniors in high school, and seniors who just graduated. The Pre-Veterinary Medicine and Veterinary Technology programs are only for rising juniors and seniors.
pay_detail: $45 application fee. Listed fees: 2-week programs $4,119 residential or $2,337 commuter; 3-week $6,125 or $3,397; 6-week Research Intensives $12,813 or $7,247. Some programs add a $95 materials fee. Limited need-based partial scholarships (up to $1,000) for 1 to 3 week programs.
duration: 1 to 6 weeks, depending on the program
deadline_text: Summer 2026 applications are closed (2026 deadlines were May 1 extended to May 15, May 15 and May 31 by start date). Research Intensives 2026 deadlines were March 15, extended to April 15. The site says Summer 2027 program details and applications will be available in January.
how_to_apply: Sign up for updates on the Pre-College page now. Applications for 2027 open in January. They are reviewed on a rolling basis. Scholarship applications use the same online system.
notes: Expensive. This is a college course experience, not a job. The page also lists year-round college prep workshops (fall 2026 workshops are open).

name: Teen Art Collective
org: Museum of Contemporary Art San Diego (MCASD)
what_you_do: This is a yearlong teen program. It includes workshops and visits from artists and museum staff. You get studio time and critiques. The program ends with a teen-organized exhibition and public event.
who_can_apply: 11th and 12th grade students from San Diego. The page says the group draws teens from across San Diego County. Limited to 25 students.
pay_detail: No stipend or cost mentioned on the page.
duration: Sept 8, 2026 to June 2027; meets the 2nd and 4th Tuesday of each month, 5 to 7 p.m.
deadline_text: 2026-2027 applications were due Friday Aug 28, 2026. Next year's dates are not posted; expect a late-summer deadline.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application (one per student). Invited students get an acceptance email and onboarding documents. Questions: education@mcasd.org.
notes: Closed for 2026-2027. The program is supported in part by the California Arts Council.

name: Teen Advisory Board at MCPL
what_you_do: You are a library teen volunteer. You give feedback on programs. You help librarians plan and run events. You speak up for youth services in the county.
who_can_apply: Applicants must be 13 or in 8th grade at the time of application. They can be up to age 17 or 18 and a senior in high school.
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn Student Service Learning (SSL) hours for attending meetings.
deadline_text: No deadline stated.
how_to_apply: Complete the Teen Advisory Board Interest Form on the MCPL page; someone contacts you after it is received.
notes: Unpaid volunteer role. The page says there will be more chances to volunteer at MCPL in the coming year.

name: Maryland 4-H Youth Development
city: Statewide, Maryland (a local Extension office in each county); state center in College Park
what_you_do: Join a county 4-H club or program. It has hands-on projects, camps and STEM contests. It also has animal and environmental science, leadership and community service.
who_can_apply: The Maryland 4-H pages read do not list an age range. Programs vary by county. Contact your local Extension office to learn which clubs and programs fit your age.
pay_detail: The page says costs are kept to a minimum. No amounts are given.
duration: Year-round, ongoing
deadline_text: No single deadline. Clubs, camps and events set their own dates.
how_to_apply: Contact your local University of Maryland Extension office. Ask about clubs, camps and programs in your county. Then use the Enroll in Maryland 4-H link on the Join a Club page.
notes: Maryland 4-H Center: 8020 Greenmead Drive, College Park, MD 20740, 301-314-9070. The leadership page lists a 2026 Volunteer and Teen Forum in Ocean City in November 2026. It has workshops for adults and teens aged 13 and older.

grades: Rising high school seniors (finished grade 11, at least one semester left)
name: Maryland Boys State
org: The American Legion, Department of Maryland
what_you_do: Spend a week in a model state government. Delegates run for city and state office. They take part in a political simulation. They hear from real leaders. There are college prep sessions too.
who_can_apply: Boys who have finished their junior year of high school by the start of the session, in public, private or home school, with at least one semester left. You cannot have attended any other Boys State.
pay_detail: Free. The FAQ says there is no cost to the student or family. Sponsors such as American Legion posts pay.
duration: One week. The 2027 session is June 20 to 26, 2027
deadline_text: 2027 session: June 20 to 26, 2027 at McDaniel College. The 2026 application ran Nov 15, 2025 to May 1, 2026. The 2027 application dates are not posted yet.
how_to_apply: Apply online using the Apply now link on the Maryland Boys & Girls State site. Accepted students usually hear back in 2 to 3 weeks.
notes: Students under 17 sleep in college dorms, usually two to a room. Phones, smartphones and smartwatches are not allowed. The site recommends against driving yourself because the week is tiring. Staff are mostly veterans.

name: Maryland FFA
what_you_do: Join an FFA chapter through your school's agricultural education program. FFA builds leadership, personal growth and career skills through agriculture classes, projects and competitions.
who_can_apply: Students in a high school agricultural education program. The site says Maryland FFA has almost 3,000 student members in 50 chapters. Age and grade rules are not listed on the pages read.
pay_detail: Membership dues are not stated on the pages read. Ask your chapter advisor.
duration: School year, ongoing
deadline_text: The state site lists a deadline to confirm or add chapter affiliation membership on Oct 15, 2026 at 5 p.m. The exact time for students to join is set by each chapter.
how_to_apply: Ask your school whether it has an agricultural education program and FFA chapter. The Maryland FFA home page has a Join FFA button and a chapters page.
notes: The 2026 National FFA Convention and Expo is listed on the site for Oct 20 to 24, 2026 in Indianapolis. If your school has no FFA chapter, contact the Maryland FFA office through the Contact page.

name: Maryland General Assembly Student Page Program
org: Maryland General Assembly, Department of Legislative Services
what_you_do: Serve as a page in the Maryland House or Senate in Annapolis. You serve for two separate weeks of the 2027 session. Pages hand out materials on the floor, run errands, help visitors and carry messages.
who_can_apply: Maryland residents who are seniors at a Maryland public or nonpublic high school and are at least 16 years old. You apply through the school you attend, not where you live.
pay_detail: A meal allowance of about $50 per day worked. The Page Office arranges lodging for pages from outside Anne Arundel County who ask for it. Pages pay their own travel to Annapolis.
duration: Two weeks that are not back to back during the 13-week session (second week of January to early April)
deadline_text: Each county sets its own application deadline and may have extra requirements. The 2027 session will have pages. Contact your county page coordinator now.
how_to_apply: Contact your county page coordinator. The page has a list. Get the county's application and find its deadline. The Maryland program page says the coordinator works with your high school.
notes: Each year 105 pages and 36 alternates are chosen from across the state. Program contact on the page: Tawana Offer, Tawana.Offer@mga.maryland.gov, 410-946-5120 (Student Programs). Paid work for people under 18 in Maryland needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=md for the exact permit and steps.

grades: Rising high school seniors (finished grade 11, at least one semester left)
name: Maryland Girls State
org: American Legion Auxiliary, Department of Maryland
what_you_do: Spend a week in a model state government. Girls run for city, county and state office, take part in legislative sessions and a mock trial, and learn how government works.
who_can_apply: Girls who have finished their junior year of high school by the start of the session, in public, private or home school, with at least one semester left. You cannot have attended any other Girls State.
pay_detail: Free. The FAQ says there is no cost to the student or family. Sponsors such as American Legion posts pay.
duration: One week. The 2027 session is June 20 to 25, 2027
deadline_text: 2027 session: June 20 to 25, 2027 at Salisbury University. The 2026 application ran Nov 15, 2025 to May 1, 2026. The 2027 application dates are not posted yet.
how_to_apply: Apply online using the Apply now link on the Maryland Boys & Girls State site. Accepted students usually hear back in 2 to 3 weeks.
notes: Students under 17 sleep in college dorms, usually two to a room. The Girls State page lists a Samsung American Legion Scholarship presentation on the last day.

name: Woodstock Job Corps Center
org: U.S. Department of Labor Job Corps
what_you_do: This is a free career training campus. The center page lists pre-apprentice training in bricklaying, building construction and carpentry. It also lists Clinical Medical Assistant. More programs are under See More.
who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must be low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules. You must meet background rules. The pages read do not explain the rules for applicants under 18.
pay_detail: Free. The national site says Job Corps covers housing, meals, basic medical care and a living allowance. The living allowance amount is not stated on the pages read.
duration: Not stated on the pages read
deadline_text: Open enrollment: you can start at any time. The process usually takes about two months.
how_to_apply: Make a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Fill out the application. Upload the documents that show you are eligible. Then connect with an admissions representative. Call 800-733-5627 with questions.
notes: Center address: 10900 Old Court Rd, Woodstock, MD 21163. No closure notice showed on the pages read on 2026-10-09. The application asks for ID, Social Security number and proof of income. Only enter these on the official jobcorps.gov site, with a parent or guardian. A parent should ask an admissions representative about the rules for 16 and 17 year olds.

name: Teen Advisory Group (TAG), Menlo Park Library
org: City of Menlo Park, Library and Community Services
what_you_do: Members help promote and improve the library's teen programs and materials. They plan events. They help with library projects. Members earn volunteer hours.
who_can_apply: Applicants should be in grades 7-12. The page does not state a residency requirement.
pay_detail: Volunteer. Members earn volunteer hours; the page does not say how many.
deadline_text: Rolling membership. The page is accepting applications for new members and states no deadline.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application linked from the library's Teen services page. Questions to David Jimenez, Librarian I, 650-330-2528 or djimenez@menlopark.gov.
notes: Meets the 1st and 3rd Thursdays, 4:30-5:30 pm, at Menlo Park Library (800 Alma St.), and the 1st and 3rd Wednesdays, 4-5 pm, at Belle Haven Library (100 Terminal Ave.). Members may attend one or both. The page is undated and is the only source; older M-A Chronicle articles describe pandemic-era activities and a different meeting pattern, so confirm the schedule with the librarian before the first meeting.

name: Youth Advisory Committee (YAC), City of Menlo Park
org: City of Menlo Park, Library and Community Services Department
what_you_do: Teens advise the Parks and Recreation Commission and city staff on youth needs, activities and programs, and help plan youth services. Members serve a one-year term.
grades: Entering grades 9-12 for the upcoming academic year
who_can_apply: Must be a City of Menlo Park resident and be entering grades 9-12 for the upcoming academic year and committee term.
pay_detail: Not stated on the page. Treated as unpaid committee service; confirm with the city.
duration: One-year term, September through May. About 6 hours per month for meetings and events.
deadline_text: Closed for 2026-27. The 2026-27 window ran May through July 2026 (page lists a July 17, 2026 deadline). The next window is not announced.
how_to_apply: Submit the YAC application form and supplemental questionnaire to the Library and Community Services Department. Staff review applications, schedule interviews and make the final selection.
notes: Competitive, and closed now. Members must attend at least 75 percent of meetings. Contact Da'Shawn Williams, Recreation Coordinator, 650-330-2248. The page lists two email addresses (dlwilliams@menlopark.org and dlwilliams@menlopark.gov); confirm which is current. An older city notice said about 8 hours per month; the current page says about 6. The page does not mention pay, so we list it as unpaid; confirm with the city.

name: Civil Air Patrol Cadets, Merced County Composite Squadron 147
org: Civil Air Patrol, Merced County Composite Squadron 147
what_you_do: Join the local Civil Air Patrol squadron's cadet program. Cadets across the country learn leadership. They also learn aerospace, fitness and character. They do things like flying, contests and summer encampments. There is also a Cyber and STEM Badge Program.
who_can_apply: The squadron welcomes all community members ages 12 to 18. They join its cadet program.
pay_detail: Civil Air Patrol says annual dues are $25 to $50 depending on location, and a fully active cadet may spend $300 to $600 in the first year (minus financial help). The squadron page does not state its own dues.
duration: Ongoing. Nationally the ideal time is a weekly meeting of about two hours, one Saturday event a month and a week long summer encampment. The squadron's meeting day and time are not listed.
deadline_text: No deadline. You can ask to join any time.
how_to_apply: Fill in the contact box on the squadron's Join Us page with your contact information and a short description of your interests. Email: christopher.ince@cawgcap.org. The squadron meets at 3515 Hardstand Ave, Atwater, CA 95301.
notes: Confirm first: the squadron pages do not list meeting times, dues or the first visit steps. The national Civil Air Patrol cadet page says cadets can join at ages 12 through 18.

name: K-12 Concurrent Enrollment (Merced College)
what_you_do: Take real Merced College classes while you are still in high school, tuition free (limitations may apply). Talk to your high school counselor about which courses fit your schedule.
grades: K-12 students (high school students check with a counselor)
who_can_apply: K-12 students. Ask your high school counselor if you are eligible. English C1000 is only open to eligible 11th and 12th graders. K-8 students need a written recommendation from their principal or designee. They also need current transcripts.
pay_detail: K-12 students can enroll in Merced College classes tuition free (limitations may apply). Some physical activity courses need an extra K-12 Permit, and some fees may still apply.
duration: By semester, including summer
deadline_text: No dates are listed on the page. Registration timing is on the College's When is Registration page.
