who_can_apply: Girls in Pennsylvania. The pages read do not state grade, citizenship or cost rules, so check the application.
pay_detail: No pay. The page says it is free in most cases; you may pay only for your own travel to Shippensburg University. Bring some cash for snacks and shirts sold during the week.
duration: One week in June
deadline_text: The home page lists a 2027 application and the dates 20-25 June 2026. The only deadline posted is old (May 20, 2023). No 2027 deadline is stated.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply tab on the Keystone Girls State site (the home page links an application for 2027). The old FAQ says to print and mail the form, then fill out a parent packet before camp. Check with a local Auxiliary unit for sponsorship.
notes: Girls only. The FAQ on the site is still from 2023, so confirm this year's dates, deadline and cost with the program before you plan. The national Auxiliary list shows June 21 to June 26, 2026 while the state site shows 20-25 June 2026.

name: Pennsylvania Outdoor Corps, Youth Summer Program
org: Pennsylvania Department of Conservation and Natural Resources, with the Student Conservation Association
city: Pennsylvania (crews in 18 cities, including Philadelphia and Pittsburgh)
what_you_do: Join a small crew in state parks and forests for six weeks. You build trails, protect habitats and improve park spaces, with adult mentors.
who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18 at the start of the program. High school students. Crews are based in cities across Pennsylvania.
pay_detail: $17.31 per hour (2026). Lunch, safety gear and daily transport from a central meeting spot in your city are provided.
duration: 6 weeks, Monday to Friday 7 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. (2026: June 29 to August 7)
deadline_text: 2026 dates were June 29 to August 7, 2026. No 2027 dates or deadline are posted on the page read.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Student Conservation Association (SCA) website. The state page links to the current openings. It links to the application too. You can email paoutdoorcorps@thesca.org.
notes: Crew locations change by year; check the SCA page for this year's list. Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.

name: Peralta Colleges Dual Enrollment (Laney, Merritt, Berkeley City, College of Alameda)
what_you_do: Take free college classes while in high school, on a Peralta campus or through classes arranged with your school. Courses go on your permanent college transcript.
who_can_apply: High school students from Oakland, Berkeley and Alameda. Needs counselor and parent or guardian signatures on the High School Special Enrollment Form.
pay_detail: Tuition and fees excused. Unit caps: CCAP 15 units fall or spring; other dual enrollment 11 units fall or spring; 9 units in summer.
duration: Per term (fall, spring, summer)
deadline_text: No deadlines posted. Register each term.
how_to_apply: Meet your counselor, apply to a Peralta college, submit the High School Special Enrollment Form, give transcript and photo ID, meet a college counselor, then register.
notes: Peralta also runs a free Summer Institute for Bay Area high schoolers including incoming 9th graders (2026 dates were June 22 to July 31; no application deadline posted). The old OUSD page mentions a stipend; the Peralta page does not.

name: Summer Youth Enrichment Program (SYEP)
org: Prince George's County Government, Office of Human Resources Management
what_you_do: You get a paid 6-week summer job. The job is with Prince George's County Government or a county partner. You get job readiness training and career exploration.
who_can_apply: Young people ages 14 to 24 in Prince George's County. Placements are by random lottery. The county's main SYEP pages were blocked for my reader, so residency and work-eligibility rules are not confirmed here.
pay_detail: Hourly and stipend opportunities are available (rate not stated in the county release I could read).
duration: 6 weeks (Jul 6 to Aug 14 in 2026)
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: applications Mar 1 to Mar 31, 2026; program Jul 6 to Aug 14, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.
how_to_apply: Apply online at syep.mypgc.us during the spring window. Eligible applicants are entered in a random lottery for a placement. Questions: syep@co.pg.md.us or 301-883-6200 (from the county release).
notes: Facts come from the County Executive's official March 1, 2026 bulletin; the county SYEP web pages returned Access Denied to my reader, so confirm at syep.mypgc.us. Highly in demand, so apply the day the window opens. Maryland rule (Maryland Department of Labor): work permits are required for all minors under 18 to work in Maryland, issued only after a job offer.

name: Youth volunteers at Summer Playtime and Summer Day Camps
org: M-NCPPC Department of Parks and Recreation, Prince George's County
what_you_do: You can volunteer at a Summer Playtime program at age 14. Or volunteer at a Summer Day Camp at age 15. You work 12 to 15 hours a week. You earn student service learning hours.
who_can_apply: Youth must reach the required age on or before May 31. It is 14 for Summer Playtime and 15 for Summer Day Camps. Youth cannot volunteer at a site where a younger sibling or child is a registered participant. Ages 15 and older need a criminal background history check.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Approved for Prince George's County Public Schools Student Service Learning hours.
duration: 12 to 15 hours per week
deadline_text: Volunteer applications are accepted online from March 1-May 1. The page gives no year.
how_to_apply: Sign up through the Volunteer Opportunities page of pgparks.com. Each youth may volunteer at only one Summer Playtime or Summer Day Camp site. Transportation is not provided.
notes: Dates for the 2027 season are not posted on the page. Unpaid volunteering, so no work permit.

name: M-NCPPC Youth Advisory Council (YAC)
org: M-NCPPC Department of Parks and Recreation, Prince George's County
what_you_do: You join about 20 high school youth. You advise the parks department. You plan teen events and community service projects. You join leadership conferences and field trips.
who_can_apply: About 20 high school-age youth who live in Prince George's County. No other rule is stated on the page.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Members earn student service learning credits or community service hours.
duration: School year; meetings in person at community centers and online
deadline_text: No application deadline stated.
how_to_apply: Email your name, resume, school information and a list of extracurricular activities to the contact named on the page (301-446-3416 for questions).
notes: The same page lists other teen programs (Teen Arts Council, Teen Vocal Showcase for ages 10 to 18, Teen Nights for ages 10 to 17). Unpaid, so no work permit.

name: Library volunteering and VolunTEEN
org: Prince George's County Memorial Library System
what_you_do: Help at a branch as a library, computer, facility or program aide. Or earn up to 6 service hours through VolunTEEN. Teens over the age of 15 can help in the Kids Achieve Club homework program.
who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 14 (library system rule). VolunTEEN is for grades 6 to 12. The Kids Achieve Club welcomes teens over 15. Volunteers cannot staff the Circulation or Information desks.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Student service learning hours are available.
duration: Temporary (limited) or regular (at least 6 months) schedules
deadline_text: No deadline. Kids Achieve Club interviews: June for September programs, November for January programs.
how_to_apply: Get a volunteer application from your local branch. Ask for the volunteer coordinator. For VolunTEEN, sign up through the Beanstack app.
notes: The page says volunteers must be vaccinated and that the library is accepting volunteers; check with your branch for the current rule. Unpaid volunteering, so no work permit.

name: Volunteer Program, Academy of Natural Sciences
org: Academy of Natural Sciences of Drexel University
what_you_do: You can help in collections departments and the Patrick Center lab. You can help with Bird Safe Philly, a bird-collision program. You can also help with Nature at Noon walks. Roles vary. Not all are open to teens.
who_can_apply: Minimum age is 14. The page lists no teen-specific roles; ask which positions accept teens.
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Regular time from half a day to several days a week, for at least one year
deadline_text: No deadline listed.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application linked on the page, then email the Volunteer Coordinator at volunteers@ansp.org about specific openings.
notes: The page does not say which areas teens can join. Bird Safe Philly runs April to May and September to November.

name: Bloomberg Arts Internship (BAI)
what_you_do: This is a paid summer internship at an arts and culture group in Philadelphia. You get training in work skills. You get mentoring. You also go to sessions on college and career readiness.
who_can_apply: Rising high school seniors in Philadelphia. The page does not state an age range or residency proof.
pay_detail: $20+ per hour for Summer 2026, plus transportation and meal support
duration: Eight weeks, up to 35 hours a week (2026: June 19 to August 14); select interns may continue in a school-year program up to 10 hours a week
deadline_text: The page posts no intern application dates. Its only application notice is for worksite hosts: Summer 2026 applications are officially closed.
how_to_apply: The program page gives no intern application steps. Contact info@philaculture.org or 215-557-7811.
notes: Pennsylvania's Department of Labor and Industry page says children need a work permit from their school district's issuing officer. The permit is not mentioned on the program page.

name: Career Connected Learning PHL (C2L-PHL) Summer Program
org: City of Philadelphia Office of Children and Families, with JEVS Human Services
what_you_do: The City funds this program. It includes paid service learning, project-based learning and internships. You learn about careers and get mentoring. You build work skills and shadow workers on the job.
who_can_apply: Philadelphia residents ages 12 to 24. In-school youth get priority. You can apply to one program per cycle.
pay_detail: Stipend on a prepaid debit card, paid every other week; total $1,300 to $1,500 depending on the program (hourly rate not listed).
duration: Summer program (plus school-year programming)
deadline_text: Summer 2026 applications are closed. FAQ: summer applications open between March and April each year.
how_to_apply: Apply through the C2L-PHL Youth Portal (phila.gov/c2l-phl). Documents: photo ID, school records, Social Security card, birth certificate or passport, and a work permit. Not first come, first served. Help: C2LPHL@jevs.org or 833-750-5627.
notes: Application is English only; call for help in other languages. Roughly 8,000 city-funded slots a summer (per PYN's site). Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.

name: Civil Air Patrol Cadets, Northeast Philadelphia Composite Squadron
org: Civil Air Patrol, Northeast Philadelphia Composite Squadron (PA-214)
what_you_do: Go to weekly squadron meetings of the Civil Air Patrol. Cadets across the country learn leadership. They also learn aerospace, fitness and character. They do things like flying, contests and summer encampments. There is also a Cyber and STEM Badge Program.
who_can_apply: Cadets ages 12 to 18. The Pennsylvania Wing page lists Become a Cadet as ages 12 to 18.
pay_detail: Civil Air Patrol says annual dues are $25 to $50 depending on location, and a fully active cadet may spend $300 to $600 in the first year (minus financial help). The squadron page does not state its own dues.
duration: The squadron meets Fridays from 7:00 to 9:15 p.m. at the Naval Support Activity Center, 700 Robbins St, Philadelphia, PA 19111.
deadline_text: No deadline. Contact the squadron any time.
how_to_apply: The squadron page does not describe a visit process. Contact the squadron: cc214@pawg.cap.gov (squadron commander) or 215-531-2278. The wing's Join CAP page has the cadet steps.
notes: The Pennsylvania Wing lists five other squadrons in the Philadelphia area. They are Willow Grove, Liberty, Griffin, Gen Carl A Spaatz and Chester County. Ask the wing which is closest to you. The dues range and first-year cost come from the national Civil Air Patrol cadet page.

grades: Rising high school juniors and seniors with a background in biology, chemistry or research
name: Neuroscience Camp for High School Students, Drexel
org: Drexel University Graduate School of Biomedical Sciences and Professional Studies
what_you_do: This is a 10-day commuter camp. It has lectures and lab experiences. The topics are current topics in neuroscience.
who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors and seniors with a biology, chemistry or research background. Admission is competitive.
duration: 10 days, in-person commuter (2026: July 20 to 31)
deadline_text: 2026 deadline was April 3, 2026. The page says 2027 Summer Institutes information will be posted this winter.
how_to_apply: Submit transcripts and two letters of recommendation. Contact camp assistant Ipatia Daigle (ied26@drexel.edu) or director Dr. Jed Shumsky (js52@drexel.edu).
notes: Drexel runs other Summer Institutes (arts and sciences, business, engineering, design, nursing, public health); their pages did not list grades, costs or dates when read.

name: Immersion Science Program (Fox Chase Cancer Center)
what_you_do: Take an 11 week laboratory research training course on Saturdays at Fox Chase (about 30 lab hours), then present your results on week 11. The program says it is nearly all cost free for students.
who_can_apply: Students at least 16 years old who finished both high school biology and chemistry. Neither can be taken at the same time. Open to students in the Philadelphia Tri-State area. You can apply to a Philadelphia-only section.
pay_detail: Nearly all programming is cost free to participants. No pay for the winter course. Fox Chase cannot provide transportation.
duration: 11 weeks of Saturday sessions from early January to mid March: Section 1 meets 8:30 to 11:30 a.m. and Section 2 meets 12:30 to 3:30 p.m. There are 16 seats, 8 per section.
deadline_text: The application launches in mid to late October each year and stays open about 3.5 weeks. The exact 2026 dates are not posted on the page read. Interviews are in early to mid December and letters go out by email before December 31.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Google form application. It cannot be saved, so a PDF version is available to draft offline. Two letters of recommendation are required. One must come from a science or STEM teacher who has known you at least a year. Applications are blind reviewed. Then three committee members interview 20 to 25 applicants.
notes: The FAQ says the application launches in mid to late October, so it may open any day now. Check the page for the real dates. General Fox Chase number: 888-369-2427. A summer fellows track is funded by National Cancer Institute grants. Its pay and rules are not stated on the pages read.

grades: Apply as a high school freshman (grade 9)
name: STEM Scholars, The Franklin Institute
what_you_do: This is a free four-year STEM program. It starts in 9th grade. Each year has STEM programming. Rising seniors are paid for a 10-week lab research experience.
who_can_apply: Students living in Philadelphia and surrounding areas who are entering 9th grade, interested in STEM, able to commit to four years, with a 3.0 GPA (per FAQ). Non-freshmen are rarely accepted.
pay_detail: Free to students; rising seniors are paid for lab research (rate not stated). Fees covered by donors.
duration: Four years, grades 9 to 12; research window of 10 weeks between late June and early September
deadline_text: Applications for the next freshman cohort are currently closed; check back for the 2027 class. FAQ says applications usually open late September or early October and are due mid-December.
how_to_apply: Online application, essay, transcript, two recommendation letters, then an interview with Youth Programs staff.
notes: The FAQ timing and the 'currently closed' message are not fully consistent, so confirm on the page. The sister middle-school program PACTS is for grades 6 to 8.

name: Philadelphia Job Corps Center
org: U.S. Department of Labor Job Corps
city: Philadelphia, PA (campus; page lists transportation and no dorms)
what_you_do: Train for a career at no cost and work toward a high school diploma or equivalent. The center provides transportation. Training includes certified nurse assistant, clinical medical assistant, culinary arts, emergency medical technician, and more.
who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules, or have other approved status. You must meet background rules. An Admissions Representative reads your application. This person decides if you can join.
pay_detail: Free to students. The campus page lists transportation to and from campus, breakfast and lunch, basic medical care, books and supplies, and a living allowance paid in cash twice a month.
duration: Not stated on the pages read
deadline_text: No deadline posted. You start by making a MyJobCorps account on the Job Corps website.
how_to_apply: Create a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Finish the application. Then an Admissions Representative sets up an interview. They review your documents and a background check. They also help you pick a campus.
notes: Mostly fits teens 16 and up who are out of school or want a different path. Housing: the Philadelphia campus page lists transportation and no dorms. A center being listed on the Job Corps site does not prove it is enrolling right now, so confirm with an Admissions Representative. The training list above comes from the center's training page and may not be complete. Whether a state work permit applies was not checked.

name: Dr. Charis Eng Monell Science Apprenticeship Program (MSAP)
what_you_do: Work full time for eight weeks on a research project with a Monell scientist. The program is described as paid, and apprentices cannot work more than 35 hours a week.
grades: Currently enrolled in high school or an undergraduate school
who_can_apply: Students now in high school or college from the greater Philadelphia area, including Camden, NJ. You must be able to prove you can work in the United States. No age or grade is stated. The committee gives strong preference to students from groups underrepresented in science.
pay_detail: Described as paid. The amount is not stated on the pages read.
duration: The program page says eight weeks of paid full-time structured research. The 2026 program ran June 15 to July 31, 2026, which is shorter than eight weeks, so confirm the length. The page does not give the 2027 dates.
deadline_text: The page says applications for the Summer 2027 program will open in October 2026. The deadline is not posted yet.
how_to_apply: Use the MSAP Applications page on monell.org when it opens. Sign up for Monell's newsletter for updates. Questions: AcademicAffairs@monell.org or 267-519-4700. About 200 applications come in each year. 18 to 24 students are usually enrolled.
notes: Minors do not need working papers to apply. They must get them after they are admitted. They come from the School District of Philadelphia, per the Monell FAQ. The Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry says minors under 18 need a work permit from their school district's issuing officer. Monell does not provide housing or meals. Students must commit to the full program with no vacations.

name: Art Education high school programs (Mural Arts Philadelphia)
what_you_do: Take part in an art program that meets twice a week at a high school site, in school or after school. The page says students can go on to apply for scholarships, internships and jobs in the creative field.
who_can_apply: Young people ages 14 to 22 at the high school sites. Ages 10 to 13 are served at middle school sites. A parent or guardian must sign and provide extra information before a youth under 18 can be enrolled.
pay_detail: Cost and pay are not stated on the pages read. The page says students can later apply for scholarships, internships and jobs in the creative field.
duration: Twice a week. The 2026 to 27 school year programs begin in late September 2026 (the page says they end in early June and prints the year 2026, which looks like a typo for 2027).
deadline_text: Rolling admission is open. The page says the fall session begins in late September 2026.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Student Inquiry Form on the Mural Arts enroll page. It is not an application and does not confirm enrollment. An Art Education staff member follows up about classes near you. Contact: natalie.gearin@muralarts.org or (215) 685-0750.
notes: The pages say 3 high school sites and 6 middle school sites on the enroll page but 16 sites in total on the program page, so ask which site is near you. Mural Arts also has paid summer work experience through Career Connected Learning (see the C2L PHL card). Ask whether classes are free. Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.

name: Become a Lifeguard, Philadelphia Parks and Recreation
what_you_do: You train for free. You earn Red Cross lifeguard certification. Then you work as a lifeguard at a city pool through the summer.
who_can_apply: You must be 16 or older to work as a city lifeguard; you can attend the screening at 15.
pay_detail: Starts at $16.85 per hour, about 35 hours a week from June through August. Red Cross certification is free for ages 16 to 24 who work at a Parks and Rec pool.
duration: June through August, about 35 hours a week; free training runs year-round
deadline_text: Free training is offered year-round; reserve a slot on Eventbrite.
how_to_apply: Choose a pool and contact its supervisor, train with Aquatics staff to pass the screening, then finish the Red Cross certification and pre-employment steps. Contact: lifeguard@phila.gov.
notes: Free training is at Lincoln High School and Friends Select School. Pennsylvania's Department of Labor and Industry page says children need a work permit from their school district's issuing officer; workers under 16 also need a parent statement (Form LLC-75).

name: Parks and Rec Summer Youth Employment Program
what_you_do: You can work at recreation centers, playgrounds and Playstreets. You can also work on special initiatives. You help younger children. You build communication and leadership skills.
who_can_apply: Youth and young adults ages 14 to 24. Residency is not stated on this page (the parent C2L-PHL program requires Philadelphia residency).
pay_detail: Not stated on the page
duration: Summer
deadline_text: The page still says registration closed for the C2L-PHL Summer 2025 program. No 2026 or 2027 dates posted.
how_to_apply: Not described on this page; positions come through C2L-PHL. Questions: PPRC2L@phila.gov or 215-683-3683.
notes: Check the C2L-PHL listing for the actual application. The page I read had not been updated after Summer 2025. Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry says work permits are required for minors under 18 hired to fill a position; the Parks and Rec page itself does not mention permits.

name: Provost's Summer Mentorship Program (Penn)
what_you_do: Spend four weeks on Penn's campus. Pair up with one of five Penn graduate and professional schools to see careers up close. Get lessons on financial literacy, study skills, time management, SAT prep and personal statements. It usually ends with a college fair.
grades: Currently 9th or 10th grade (entering 10th or 11th grade in fall 2027)
who_can_apply: Students who live in Philadelphia. You must go to a Philadelphia public, Catholic, private or charter high school. You need a minimum GPA of 3.0.
pay_detail: Cost and stipend are not stated on the pages read, so ask the program before you plan around either.
duration: Four weeks, on campus. Exact summer 2027 dates are not posted.
deadline_text: The page says the Summer Mentorship Program for 2027 will begin taking applications in January 2027. The deadline is not posted yet.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply page on the program site when it opens in January 2027. You will need a high school transcript with fall 2026 grades. You need a 250 word essay about yourself and your interest in the program. You need an up to date vaccine record.
notes: The two pages word the grade rule differently (currently 9th or 10th on the apply page, entering 10th or 11th in fall 2027 on the main page); they describe the same group. Office: St. Leonard's Court, Suite 110, 3819 Chestnut Street, Philadelphia, PA 19104; contact form at https://vpse.upenn.edu/smp/contact-us/.

grades: Academies and Online Seminars: current 9th to 11th grade. Pre-College: current 10th to 11th grade.
name: Penn Arts and Sciences High School Summer Programs
org: University of Pennsylvania, Penn LPS High School Programs
what_you_do: Summer Academies (2 or 3 weeks, non-credit, residential), Pre-College (residential or online, for credit) and Online Seminars on topics like biomedical research, economics, forensic science and neuroscience.
who_can_apply: Current 9th to 11th graders (Pre-College: 10th to 11th).
pay_detail: 2026 tuition: 2-week Academy $6,700; 3-week Academy $10,050; Pre-College Residential $15,192 to $23,604; Pre-College Online $8,692 or $14,300; Online Seminars $2,950. $1,500 deposit and $100 application fee (waived for School District of Philadelphia applicants).
duration: 2 to 6 weeks depending on program (2026 Academies: July 11 to August 1)
deadline_text: 2026: May 1 for Academies and Pre-College Residential/Online Session I; June 1 for Online Seminars and Pre-College Online Session II. Rolling admissions. 2027 dates not posted.
how_to_apply: Online application from the student: essays (400 words each), transcript, recommendations. For the scholarship, say you attend a School District of Philadelphia school and fill in the scholarship section.
notes: There are no scholarships for the Pre-College programs. Contact hsprogs@sas.upenn.edu or 215-746-2309.

grades: Rising 9th to 12th grade (Junior PYNtern rising 9th to 10th; Senior PYNtern rising 11th to 12th)
name: PYNtern Program
what_you_do: This is paid work-based learning. It includes classroom training in professional skills. You get mentoring and career coaching. Rising juniors and seniors do about 100 hours at a paid worksite in the city.
who_can_apply: Young people ages 14 to 18, primarily rising 9th to 12th graders. The page does not state a residency rule.
pay_detail: Up to $1,500 for a 6 to 8 week experience, depending on hours and milestones
duration: 6 to 8 weeks per cohort (page also says experiences last 6 to 12 weeks)
deadline_text: Summer cohort applications open early March; Fall/Winter cohort open early August; Winter/Spring cohort open in November. Page says Now Recruiting for Summer + Fall 2026.
how_to_apply: Use Apply Now or the interest form on the page (name, contact, current grade, cohort, three career fields). Phone 267-502-3800 or info@pyninc.org.
notes: About 400 internship slots a year across cohorts. The city's large summer jobs program is C2L-PHL, a separate application. Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.

name: Career and Technical Education (CTE), School District of Philadelphia
what_you_do: Career programs in over 43 occupational areas (healthcare, IT, culinary, construction and more), a three-year course of study with work-based learning such as internships and apprenticeships.
who_can_apply: District high school students starting in 10th grade. Middle schoolers choose a CTE program on their School Selection application; high schoolers can join if their school has the program and space allows.
pay_detail: School program; the page does not say whether internships are paid.
duration: Typically 3 years, 1,080 hours of instruction; some programs 1 or 2 years
deadline_text: Follow the School Selection timeline for middle schoolers; high schoolers ask their counselor.
how_to_apply: Middle school: pick schools that offer your CTE program on the School Selection application. High school: talk to your school counselor.
notes: The page notes that students ages 14 to 17 need working papers to work. Which schools offer which programs is in the CTE Programs List.

name: Counselor-in-Training Program, Camp Schuylkill
what_you_do: You volunteer as a counselor-in-training. You work with the Camp Schuylkill nature day camp. You help lead younger campers.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17. Positions are limited.
pay_detail: Volunteer program with no fee listed; hours can count as school or organization service hours.
duration: Two full weeks required; may be asked to work up to three weeks; one Saturday training in May
deadline_text: 2026 deadline was March 31, 2026. Camp Schuylkill runs on a weekly schedule from June 21 to August 13, 2027.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Google Form on the camp page, including a one-page essay (why you want to volunteer as a CIT, experience with children, what you enjoy about nature).
notes: Camp is at 8480 Hagy's Mill Road, Philadelphia, PA 19128. The page's date line looks like a typo (June 15, 2025 to August 14, 2026), so confirm dates when the 2027 application posts.

name: Wildlife Clinic Support Volunteer, Schuylkill Center
what_you_do: You support the wildlife clinic. The clinic treats injured and orphaned wild animals. Clinic Support is for ages 16 and up. Animal Care requires age 18.
who_can_apply: Clinic Support volunteers must be 16 or older (Animal Care requires 18+). Must attend a training session, sign the volunteer agreement and finish online ethics and safety courses.
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Minimum one 4-hour shift a week (about 20 hours a month)
deadline_text: 2026 in-person info sessions were February 7 and February 28; virtual sessions as needed. Fill out the application to hear about future sessions.
how_to_apply: Complete the Wildlife Clinic volunteer Google Form. It is linked on the page.
notes: The general volunteer page says regular volunteers who work with children need Pennsylvania child abuse and criminal history clearances (free for volunteers).

name: High School Program in Biomedical Research (Wistar Institute)
what_you_do: Spend four weeks at the Wistar Institute (3601 Spruce Street) learning biomedical research, with 15 students in the program. Students attend Monday to Thursday, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.
who_can_apply: Students who are at least 16 by the program start date and have finished at least one high school science course. The program gives priority to students in the School District of Philadelphia. It strongly encourages Philadelphia high school students to apply. No grade level or residency rule is listed.
pay_detail: $1,500 stipend for finishing the program, plus SEPTA passes for travel
duration: Four weeks (the 2026 session ran July 6 to July 30). An optional three week extension in August depends on funding.
deadline_text: The 2026 program has ended. The page says to check back in January for the 2027 summer program. Last year's cycle had interviews in April and decisions in the first week of May.
how_to_apply: Send an online application. It has a personal statement of one page, single spaced. It has two letters of recommendation. One from a science teacher is preferred. It has an unofficial transcript or list of classes with grades. Finalists have a 15 minute virtual interview in April. Participants and a parent or guardian go to a mandatory orientation in June.
notes: Contacts: Jason Diaz, 215-898-3803, jdiaz@wistar.org, or Cailey Bice, 215-898-3749, cbice@wistar.org. Absences of more than two days in a row cannot be accommodated. The stipend is not called a wage on the page. Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.

name: Volun-TEENS, Philadelphia Zoo
what_you_do: Teach zoo guests about animals and conservation. You use games and hands-on activities. You build public speaking, leadership and time management skills.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17.
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: The page says to stay tuned for details about the next recruitment period; no dates listed.
how_to_apply: Email the zoo through the contact link on the volunteer page. No application link is listed.
notes: Separate options: Special Events volunteers (13+ for family events) apply through an online form; school groups of grades 9 to 12 can join Boo at the Zoo takeover shifts (those 2026 dates have passed). Docents must be 21+.

grades: Grades 6 to 12 (high school volunteers: grades 9 to 12 and at least 14)
name: Teen Volunteer Program, Piscataway Public Library
what_you_do: Help with library programs and special projects. Middle schoolers can join Adopt-a-Shelf. They help keep teen spaces and collections neat. They also advise on new purchases.
who_can_apply: Piscataway residents only. Grades 6 to 12 and at least 12 years old; high school volunteers must be in grades 9 to 12 and at least 14. Must sign a Teen Volunteer Code of Conduct at training.
pay_detail: Unpaid; earns community service hours
duration: Regularly scheduled volunteer hours after training
deadline_text: Adopt-a-Shelf: the Session 1 application period has ended; Session 2 applications open November 2 (year not stated on the page). High school volunteers attend an orientation session; check the library calendar for dates.
how_to_apply: High school: attend a library orientation session with a mandatory training video, then enroll if you meet requirements. Adopt-a-Shelf (grades 6 to 8): apply on the volunteering page when the session opens. Questions: teens@piscatawaylibrary.org (subject line Volunteer).
notes: Latecomers are not admitted to training sessions. Open only to Piscataway residents.

name: Teen Workforce Pathways (Boys & Girls Clubs of Western Pennsylvania)
org: Boys & Girls Clubs of Western Pennsylvania
what_you_do: Get hands-on experiences, mentors and a look at real careers in several industries. Join councils and internship pathways. Get help with resumes and interview prep through the Career Works High program.
who_can_apply: Teens at Club locations that offer Workforce Pathways: Carnegie, Estelle S. Campbell (Lawrenceville), Shadyside, Downtown and McKeesport. The page does not give an age range.
pay_detail: Cost and pay are not stated on the pages read, and the page does not mention paid work. Financial assistance is available for Club membership.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No dates are posted on the page.
how_to_apply: Use the Returning Teen or New Teen registration link on the Workforce Pathways page. Or use Register Now at bgcwpa.org/registration. Financial assistance is available. See the Financial Assistance page. Phone: (412) 782-5710. Email: contact@bgcwpa.org.
notes: Confirm first: ages, cost, schedule and whether any work is paid are not on the pages read. The Clubs also run two Club Teen Centers (Downtown and McKeesport).

name: Summer Camp Teen Volunteers (Carnegie Museums)
org: Carnegie Museums of Pittsburgh (Natural History, Art and Powdermill Nature Reserve)
what_you_do: Help museum staff and camp educators. You help with learning activities that support campers. The camps are run by three groups. They are the Carnegie Museum of Natural History, the Carnegie Museum of Art and Powdermill Nature Reserve.
who_can_apply: Natural History camps: teens 14 and older. Powdermill Nature Reserve camps: ages 14 to 19. Art museum camps: 16 and older. Each museum has its own application form.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role
duration: Summer camp season. Hours and camp dates are not stated on the volunteer pages.
deadline_text: The Natural History form says the application period has closed and to check back in early 2027 for the next cycle. Dates for the next cycle are not posted.
how_to_apply: Use the museum's own teen camp volunteer application form. It is linked from the Carnegie Museums volunteer page. There is one form each for Natural History, Powdermill and Art. Questions: volunteers@carnegiemuseums.org or 412-353-4680.
notes: The apply link above is the Natural History form. The Art museum form is https://form.jotform.com/230685138792162 and the Powdermill form is https://form.jotform.com/230595011446148. The Natural History page also lists a Teen Advisory Board with an interest form (https://form.jotform.com/243505851081150); its ages are not stated. The Kamin Science Center teen volunteers are a separate card.

name: Civil Air Patrol Cadets, Allegheny County Composite Squadron
org: Civil Air Patrol, Allegheny County Composite Squadron
what_you_do: Go to weekly squadron meetings of the Civil Air Patrol. Cadets across the country learn leadership. They also learn aerospace, fitness and character. They do things like flying, contests and summer encampments. There is also a Cyber and STEM Badge Program.
who_can_apply: Cadets ages 12 to 18. The Pennsylvania Wing page lists Become a Cadet as ages 12 to 18.
pay_detail: Civil Air Patrol says annual dues are $25 to $50 depending on location, and a fully active cadet may spend $300 to $600 in the first year (minus financial help). The squadron page does not state its own dues.
duration: The squadron meets Tuesdays from 6:30 to 8:30 p.m. at Baldwin High School, 4653 Clairton Blvd, Pittsburgh, PA 15236.
deadline_text: No deadline. Contact the squadron any time.
how_to_apply: The squadron page links a Google Form for people interested in joining and the wing's Become a Cadet page. It lists no squadron email or phone. The Pennsylvania Wing headquarters can be reached at 717-220-3517 or hq@pawg.cap.gov.
notes: The Pennsylvania Wing lists other squadrons in the Pittsburgh area. They are Golden Triangle, Jimmy Stewart, Washington, Beaver Falls and Butler. Ask the wing which is closest to you. The dues range and first-year cost come from the national Civil Air Patrol cadet page.

name: CS Scholars
what_you_do: You spend four weeks living on the CMU campus. You learn computer science through classes and group projects. You hear faculty lectures and visit tech companies. All costs are covered.
who_can_apply: Students at least 16 by the program start, in 10th grade when applying, and U.S. citizens or permanent residents with a green card. Meant for students who lack access or resources in computer science.
pay_detail: Fully funded: tuition, housing and meals are free; limited travel help for families with transportation barriers
duration: 4 weeks, June 26 to July 24, 2027, residential
deadline_text: Application deadline February 1, 2027. Decisions released April 1, 2027.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the CMU Pre-College application portal by February 1, 2027. Residential only; full participation required.
notes: Status is unconfirmed only because the application opening date is not posted; the 2027 deadlines are confirmed on the program pages (the apply portal could not be read). Limited spots. The admission page lists two different dates for this application (February 1 and March 1, 2027); the program page and the deadlines table both say February 1, 2027, so apply by then. Completers may be invited back to AI Scholars.

name: Pre-College Programs (paid tracks)
what_you_do: Live on or commute to the CMU campus for 3 to 6 weeks. Study architecture, art, design, drama or music. Also study computational biology or writing. You can also study culture. Pick the National High School Game Academy or college summer courses.
grades: 10th or 11th grade at time of application
who_can_apply: High school students at least 16 years old by June 26, 2027 who are in 10th or 11th grade when they apply.
pay_detail: 2026 prices ran from about $5,999 (3-week music, commuter) to $14,688 (summer session, residential, 2 courses), plus a $75 application fee and an $800 enrollment deposit. 2027 prices are posted in November 2026. Full scholarships for students with financial need.
duration: 3 to 6 weeks depending on the program (summer 2027 starts June 26)
deadline_text: Scholarship application deadline February 1, 2027 (decisions April 1, 2027). Basic application deadline March 1, 2027 (rolling decisions).
how_to_apply: Apply online through the CMU Pre-College application portal. The scholarship option is only considered under the February 1, 2027 deadline.
notes: Status is unconfirmed only because the application opening date is not posted; the 2027 deadlines are confirmed on the program pages (the apply portal could not be read). Expensive; shown so families know the cost and the scholarship route. The three fully funded programs (AI Scholars, CS Scholars, SAMS) cost nothing. Check the cost page again in November 2026 for 2027 prices.

name: Summer Academy for Math and Science (SAMS)
what_you_do: Six weeks on the CMU campus taking math and science courses, doing a STEM research project, and getting college application help. Fully funded and merit based.
who_can_apply: Students at least 16 years old by the program start who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents and in 11th grade when they apply. The program focuses on students underrepresented in STEM.
pay_detail: No cost to scholars beyond travel to and from Pittsburgh
duration: 6 weeks in person, June 26 to August 7, 2027, plus a short virtual jumpstart June 21 and 22, 2027
deadline_text: Application deadline February 1, 2027. Decisions released April 1, 2027.
how_to_apply: The application opening date is not posted; apply online through the CMU Pre-College application portal by February 1, 2027. Residential only; scholars must attend the full program.
notes: Status is unconfirmed only because the application opening date is not posted; the 2027 deadlines above are confirmed on the program pages (the apply portal itself could not be read, it needs JavaScript). Competitive and limited spots. The page gives no application opening date. Scholars cannot take other summer programs that overlap. Questions: cmu-sams@andrew.cmu.edu.

name: Pittsburgh Job Corps Center
org: U.S. Department of Labor Job Corps
what_you_do: Live on campus. You train for a career at no cost. You also earn a high school diploma or equivalent. Training includes highway construction. It includes cement masonry. Phlebotomy is another. So is clinical medical assistant. There are more.
who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules, or have other approved status. You must meet background rules. An Admissions Representative reads your application. This person decides if you can join.
pay_detail: Free to students. The campus page lists furnished dorms, meals, basic medical care, books and supplies, and a living allowance paid in cash twice a month.
duration: Not stated on the pages read
deadline_text: No deadline posted. You start by making a MyJobCorps account on the Job Corps website.
how_to_apply: Create a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Finish the application. Then an Admissions Representative sets up an interview. They review your documents and a background check. They also help you pick a campus.
notes: Mostly fits teens 16 and up who are out of school or want a different path. Housing: dorms are listed on the campus page. A center being listed on the Job Corps site does not prove it is enrolling right now, so confirm with an Admissions Representative. The training list above comes from the center's training page and may not be complete. Whether a state work permit applies was not checked.

name: Teen Volunteer Program
org: Kamin Science Center (formerly Carnegie Science Center)
what_you_do: Greet visitors, help with exhibit demos and support science programs. Full training is provided. No science background is needed.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18. Must be at least 14 by the application deadline. Late applications are not considered.
pay_detail: Volunteer, unpaid
duration: Summer Teen Program and School Year Teen Program (hours per week not stated)
deadline_text: Summer Teen Program: applications open in January, deadline March 1. School Year Teen Program: applications June 1 to August 1 only. Both were closed on the day this page was read; the posted pattern is by month, with no year.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application (or download one to email or mail) during the window. Selected teens are interviewed and must complete an orientation.
notes: Teens accepted twice a year (summer and school year). The next summer window should open in January; confirm on the page.

name: Summer Learn & Earn
org: Partner4Work, Allegheny County and City of Pittsburgh
what_you_do: Work a paid summer job at a local business, nonprofit or community group. You get coaching on workplace skills and career paths.
who_can_apply: Young people ages 14 to 23 in Allegheny County and the City of Pittsburgh. Income and residency requirements apply (details on the application).
pay_detail: Paid wages (hourly rate not stated on the program page)
duration: Tier 1 and 2: June 22nd, 2026 - August 7th, 2026. Hours per week are not stated on the page.
deadline_text: 2026 applications ran March 2 to June 5, 2026 and are closed. The page says applications are accepted in the spring; 2027 dates are not posted yet.
how_to_apply: Apply online through Partner4Work during the spring application window (new participants and returning participants use different links). A complete eligible application does not guarantee a placement, so apply early.
notes: Questions: summer@partner4work.org or (412) 932-2950. A separate Year-Round Learn & Earn (fall, winter, spring work sessions) serves ages 16 to 23 in the City of Pittsburgh but only for people who already finished a summer. The program page does not mention a work permit; the Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry says work permits are required for minors under 18, so ask your school or the program how to get one.

name: Teen Volunteer Program
what_you_do: You help run bird shows and lorikeet feedings. You help at summer camp. You lead education cart activities. You prepare enrichment for the birds. Staff mentor you each day.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17 interested in animal-related careers (age counted as of June 1, 2026 for the 2026 session). Must commit to at least 8 of the 10 days in the chosen session.
pay_detail: Volunteer, unpaid
duration: 10-day sessions; orientation with a parent or guardian in late May
deadline_text: The 2026 application period has closed. For 2026 the group interviews were April 11 and April 18, 2026 and the orientation was May 30, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.
how_to_apply: Submit the volunteer application when it reopens, attend an in-person group interview, and attend orientation with a parent or guardian.
notes: Questions go to the volunteer contact on the National Aviary volunteer page.

name: EcoLeader Academy
what_you_do: Take a seven-week course at Phipps. Topics are climate change, energy, pollution, food, environmental justice and green careers. It has classes, workshops and service projects. It ends with a Youth Garden Summit.
who_can_apply: Students ages 14 to 19 who have finished at least one year of high school. You pick one of two weekly groups (Wednesday or Thursday) and must attend all of the dates.
pay_detail: Free to join. Participants receive a stipend (amount not stated on the page).
duration: Seven-week course, one afternoon a week (12:30 to 4:30 p.m.) at Phipps, plus a Youth Garden Summit at the end
deadline_text: The 2026 group is closed. The page offers a form to be told when the next group opens. The 2026 classes ran mid June to late July.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application form on the Phipps page when the next group opens. Use the sign-up form on that page to be notified. Questions go to the high school programs coordinator at amule@phipps.conservatory.org or 412-622-6915 ext. 3804.
notes: The page lists two different dates for the final Youth Garden Summit, so confirm with Phipps. The stipend is not described as a job on the page. Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.

name: Summer Camp Teen Volunteers (Phipps)
what_you_do: Help camp instructors design and prepare crafts. Work with children ages 2 to 12. Clean up after daily activities at Phipps summer camps.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18 who enjoy working with children. You must be able to get Pennsylvania Act 33/34 clearances. Phipps pays back the fees.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role. Clearance fees are reimbursed.
duration: Summer camps held June to August. Hours are not stated.
deadline_text: The volunteer page says applications are due Thursday, October 22, 2026. The page does not say whether that date applies to teen volunteers, so ask Phipps. Camps run June to August.
how_to_apply: The page says the first step for volunteers is to fill out an application. Accepted applicants then go to an interview, orientation and placement meetings. The page does not give a form just for teens. Email the volunteer coordinator listed on the Phipps volunteer page to ask. That is Deb Knorr, dknorr@phipps.conservatory.org.
notes: Confirm first. The volunteer page gives no teen deadline or teen form. Ask Phipps for the current age rule and dates before you plan around this.

name: Gene Team
org: University of Pittsburgh, Department of Biological Sciences
what_you_do: Spend weekdays in a Pitt lab working on a current research project with other high school students, with Pitt faculty nearby for help. Weekly sessions cover applying to college.
grades: Finished one year of high school biology
who_can_apply: Students from high schools in the Pittsburgh region who have completed one year of high school biology. The page does not state an age rule.
pay_detail: $1,000 honorarium, paid at the end of the program
duration: Described as a four week summer program. Summer 2027 is tentatively June 28 to July 16, Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 3 p.m.
deadline_text: Summer 2027 applications open in spring 2027 and are due at the end of March, with interviews in April and acceptance notices by mid May. The exact due date is not posted yet.
how_to_apply: The page says a link to the application will be posted when applications open. To get updates, join the email list by contacting Jess Robertson at jah99@pitt.edu. Questions: Dr. Becky Gonda, 412-383-5739, reg11@pitt.edu.
notes: No research experience is needed. Free PRT bus passes are available. The honorarium is not called a wage on the page. The page's dates (June 28 to July 16) are shorter than 'four weeks', so confirm the length. Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.

name: Public Health Science Academy
org: University of Pittsburgh School of Public Health
what_you_do: This is a four week summer program at Pitt Public Health. It has talks and panels on public health careers. It has a team research project and a poster symposium. It also has field trips. You are matched with a Pitt faculty mentor.
who_can_apply: Current 10th or 11th graders at a high school in the Greater Pittsburgh area or Western PA. You need a strong interest in science and a GPA of 3.0 or above. You must finish a biology class by the end of the school year. You must commit to the full four weeks.
pay_detail: Students who finish receive a $1,000 award at the end. Public transportation support to and from campus is provided, and transportation for field trips.
duration: Four weeks. The 2026 session ran June 22 to July 17, Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 12:30 p.m.
deadline_text: The 2026 application ran Feb 4 to March 14, 2026, and is closed. The 2027 dates are not posted yet. Expect a similar winter to March window.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It has two essays of up to 200 words each. A high school teacher must complete the recommendation form. It is uploaded at the end of the application or emailed to phsa@pitt.edu by the deadline. Incomplete applications are not considered. Applicants are told by email in mid to late March. They confirm by April 1.
notes: The main page says public high schools in one place and all high schools in another, so ask which applies to you. The award is not called a wage on the page. Applicants without a computer or reliable internet are encouraged to apply. Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.

name: Teen Volunteer Program
what_you_do: You volunteer one shift a week. The shift is in an approved area of the children's hospital. Examples are the sibling center or therapy gym. Hospital staff supervise you.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 15 to 17 (having turned 15 by June 1, 2026 for the 2026 program). Two non-relatives must complete a reference form. Needs proof of a negative TB test and a Tdap shot before orientation.
pay_detail: Volunteer, unpaid
duration: At least 8 weeks over the summer, 6 to 8 hours a week (shifts are three or four hours). Year-round spots possible after a satisfactory summer.
deadline_text: The hospital is not accepting new teen applications for this calendar year and says to check back in early January for next year's process.
how_to_apply: Check the teen program page in early January for how to submit an inquiry. Questions: chpvolunteer@chp.edu or 412-692-5185.
notes: Very high demand and limited spots. The volunteer office does not handle shadowing, internships or research requests; contact departments directly for those. Adult volunteer program is 18 and older.

name: UPMC Hillman Cancer Center Academy
org: UPMC Hillman Cancer Center and University of Pittsburgh
what_you_do: Join a mentored research team in a lab. There are nine research sites at Pitt and UPMC. It runs for about seven weeks in the summer. Topics include cancer biology, computer science and biomedical informatics.
grades: High school (seniors allowed if not taking college courses that summer)
who_can_apply: High school students in good school standing. You must be at least 15 at the program start for the computational sites (CompBio, COSBBI, Surgery). You must be at least 16 for the other sites. There is no residency rule, but out of region students must find their own housing.
pay_detail: Free to attend. Stipends are offered to qualified students from a background underrepresented in biomedicine (details are on the stipend page linked from the application site).
duration: About seven weeks. Tentative 2027 dates: June 14 to July 30, 2027.
deadline_text: Application window: December 3, 2026 to February 14, 2027.
how_to_apply: Send an online application. It has two short essays. It has one or two references, who get an email. It has a resume and a high school transcript. It has parent or guardian contact information with a digital signature. It also has your top research site choices. PDF files are preferred. In person students may need proof of vaccination.
notes: Very competitive. Another page describes it as an eight week program, so confirm the length. Questions: hillman.academy@pitt.edu or Steven Jones, 412-624-5904 (from the program's Oct 2025 profile). The stipend is not called a wage on the page. Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.

name: Youth Arts Council
what_you_do: Go behind the scenes at the museum. Meet professional artists. Learn silkscreen printing. Plan teen events such as Youth Invasion.
who_can_apply: Pittsburgh area teens ages 15 to 18 (high school students).
pay_detail: Participants receive stipends (amount not stated)
duration: Weekly Thursdays 3:30 to 6 p.m., Oct 15, 2026 to May 2027
deadline_text: Application deadline: Friday, October 9, 2026 (the day this page was read). Weekly meetings start October 15, 2026.
how_to_apply: Send in the online application by the deadline. Work samples are optional. Email teens@warhol.org with questions. Bus tickets are available for transportation.
notes: The 2026-27 deadline falls on 2026-10-09, so email teens@warhol.org to ask whether late applications are accepted. The Warhol also hires paid Student Assistants and runs a free Teen DJ Academy (ages 14 to 18, stipend) and School of Drag (ages 14 to 18); see the Teens page. Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.

name: Summer Zoo Teen Program
what_you_do: You volunteer one day a week at the zoo. You handle and care for ambassador animals. You guide guests at exhibits. You run touch tables and animal talks.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17 who are interested in animals and conservation (having turned 14 by June 1, 2026). Must commit to one day a week for at least 5 of the 7 weeks.
pay_detail: Volunteer, unpaid
duration: 7 weeks, one day a week, 9:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. (June 15 to July 31, 2027)
deadline_text: Applications for the 2027 program open December 15, 2026 and stay open through mid-January 2027. The exact closing date is not posted.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application when it opens. All applicants are interviewed in person before acceptance. Not all applicants are accepted.
notes: Volunteer role, so no pay. Contact the Volunteer Services Manager through the zoo volunteer page. The page's age requirement reads 'having turned 14 by June 1, 2026' even though it describes the 2027 program, so ask the zoo to confirm the age cutoff date. Confirm dates when applications open.

name: Planting Justice Youth Internships
what_you_do: You do a paid youth internship at an urban farm and nursery. You learn sustainable farming, food distribution and school gardens. You get job training. You get food safety certifications. Community mentors help you.
who_can_apply: No age or grade rule is stated. The program focuses on youth facing challenges such as hunger or homelessness and aims to keep them in school.
pay_detail: $17.50 per hour (page says 40+ paid internships)
deadline_text: Not posted
how_to_apply: Email your resume to jobs@plantingjustice.org. Or call the East Oakland Nursery at 510-756-6965.
notes: Ages, season and hours are not stated, so call and ask. Pay is from the program page and may change.

name: Pleasanton Youth Commission
what_you_do: Students are appointed to a city commission. They give the City Council advice. They give feedback on community issues that affect young people.
grades: Middle school, 9th grade, or 11th grade seats (fall 2026 recruitment)
who_can_apply: Must reside within Pleasanton city limits. Seats are set aside by grade: middle school, 9th grade, and 11th grade (fall 2026 ad: 3 seats each).
pay_detail: Volunteer appointed seat. No pay is stated in the recruitment ad.
deadline_text: Fall 2026 recruitment: apply by 5:00 PM on Tuesday, August 18, 2026. That deadline has passed. The next recruitment date is not posted.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the City of Pleasanton boards and commissions page (link at the bottom of the page, per the recruitment ad). Questions: Office of the City Clerk, 925-931-5027.
notes: The next recruitment date is not posted in the ad we read; deadline_confidence is last-year-pattern because the most recent cycle was fall 2026. The recruitment ad describes city commissions in general; the Youth Commission's own duties and term length were not on a page we could open, so what_you_do is based on the ad's general description.

name: San Mateo Police Cadet (Explorer) Program
what_you_do: You go to training classes and monthly meetings. You finish a required 9 week Police Cadet Academy on Sundays. You do at least 10 volunteer hours a month in community service.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 20 at appointment, enrolled in high school or college with a C average or better. Needs a valid government ID (CA ID, driver license or US passport), parent consent if under 18, and a background check.
duration: 9 week academy plus monthly service
deadline_text: No deadline posted. A recruiter contacts you after you send the application.
how_to_apply: Email the completed application to joinsmpd@cityofsanmateo.org or call the Recruiting Unit at 650-522-7629.
notes: Training classes are on the 1st and 3rd Thursday, 5 to 7 p.m. Hours count toward school service requirements. You need a flexible schedule for weekdays and weekends. FAQ is at cityofsanmateo.org/4720.

name: Hayward Police Explorer Program
what_you_do: You attend Wednesday night meetings and training. You go on ride-alongs. You help with traffic and crowd control at events. You join Explorer competitions.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 19 (not yet 19 and a half), full-time student, 2.5 GPA, must pass a background check.
deadline_text: Applications are taken twice a year, in January and July (page gives no exact dates). The next window is expected in January 2027.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application, or contact the coordinator at 510-293-5060 or Explorers@hayward-ca.gov.
notes: The page gives no closing dates, so check at the start of each window. Meetings are Wednesday nights 5 to 7pm plus training and some weekend events.

name: Morgan Hill Police Explorer Program
what_you_do: You get practical police training, volunteer at community events, and compete in statewide Explorer competitions with police scenarios. Officers and dispatchers lead the program.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 21, currently enrolled in school with a C average or better. No felony or certain misdemeanor convictions, no pending criminal cases, and you must agree to fingerprinting for a background check.
pay_detail: Free; you may buy your own uniform (help available)
deadline_text: No deadline posted.
how_to_apply: Email the Explorer application PDF to MHPD_Explorers@morganhill.ca.gov, then complete an oral board interview.
notes: Free to join, but you may need to buy a uniform and gear. Financial help is available. Expected to attend all meetings, trainings and events. Meeting times are not on the page.

name: Oakland Police Explorers
what_you_do: You go to weekly meetings with law enforcement. You do physical training and go on ride-alongs. You do community service details. You also attend conferences.
who_can_apply: High school students at least 14.5 years old, 2.0 GPA, average or better attendance and discipline, no felony or serious misdemeanor.
deadline_text: No intake dates posted. Contact the coordinator.
how_to_apply: Email Explorer Coordinator Officer Charles Stone at cstone@oaklandca.gov, or Oakland PAL (Officer Jumaal Hill) at 510-615-5758 or oaklandpal@oaklandpal.org.
notes: The page gives a minimum age of 14.5 and no upper limit. The page does not give meeting times or dates, so ask the coordinator. Oakland PD also runs the Police Activities League.

name: Pomona College Academy for Youth Success (PAYS)
what_you_do: This is a free 4-week residential summer program at Pomona College. After that, there is year-round involvement for three years. It helps local students prepare for selective colleges.
who_can_apply: Current 9th graders who live or attend high school in Los Angeles, Orange, Riverside, San Bernardino or Ventura County. First-generation, low-income, or Geometry/Integrated Math II students are considered but not required. About 30 students are admitted each year.
pay_detail: Free. Pomona College covers housing, food, activities and field-trip transportation. No stipend mentioned.
duration: 4-week residential summer (2027: June 20 to July 16), then 3 years of involvement
deadline_text: Applications open Nov 9, 2026 and are due Feb 22, 2027 (recommendations due Mar 1, 2027). Decisions Apr 16, 2027.
how_to_apply: Online New Student Application, two essays (up to 500 words each), a current-year transcript and two recommendations (one from a core subject teacher). Some applicants are interviewed. Contact PAYS@pomona.edu or (909) 607-1810.
notes: The apply page mentions both 2025-2026 and 2026-2027 in places; the 2026-2027 deadlines above are the ones listed. Confirm with the program. Pomona College is in Claremont, next to Pomona.

name: High School Volunteer Program
what_you_do: You volunteer one shift a week in the hospital. It helps you explore medical careers.
who_can_apply: Students currently in 9th, 10th or 11th grade. The page does not list an age rule.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role
duration: At least 1 year; one 3-hour shift a week (up to 3 shifts)
deadline_text: No dates posted. The same page says the hospital is currently only accepting adult volunteer applications, so check before applying.
how_to_apply: Use the 'Click here to apply for high school volunteer opportunities' link on the page, or call the hospital volunteer office to confirm if high school applications are open.
notes: CONFIRM FIRST: the page offers a high school application link but also says only adult applications are being accepted right now. Scheduled Monday to Friday shifts.

name: Pretend City Children's Museum Volunteers and Teen Programs
what_you_do: At a children's museum, you can volunteer in administration, field trips or special events. You can also lead a short activity for kids. You can be a TeensTeach or TeensTable teen presenter.
who_can_apply: Volunteers must be 12 or older. The TeensTeach and TeensTable teen programs are for ages 13 to 19.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page lists no fees.
duration: At least 3 hours a month and 15 hours a year before you sign up for training (volunteers). TeensTeach and TeensTable length is set by you.
deadline_text: No deadline. Teen program submissions are rolling and spots are limited.
how_to_apply: Volunteers: create an account and submit the individual application, read the handbook, finish the online orientation and quiz, then sign up for training. Teen programs: submit an idea through the page. Staff pick programs that fit the museum's mission and email chosen applicants.
notes: Address: 29 Hubble, Irvine, CA 92618. Volunteer questions: volunteer@pretendcity.org or 949-428-3900. The page also links a Youth Leadership Board but does not describe it.

name: Peer-to-Peer Service Collective for Teens
what_you_do: Pitch your own workshop or activity for other teens and families. If chosen, library staff help you shape it, promote it and present it at a library branch. Builds planning and public speaking skills.
who_can_apply: Current high school students in grades 9-12 who live in the five boroughs, with parental consent and NYS working papers, and who register as library volunteers.
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn community service credit for time presenting.
duration: Varies by project
deadline_text: Fall 2026 submissions are open Sept 21 to Oct 31, 2026. The spring window is Feb 1 to Feb 28, 2027. Online info session Oct 13, 2026, 5-6 pm.
how_to_apply: Complete the Idea Submission questionnaire on the library volunteer site during a submission window. The Civic Engagement Team will contact you to get your idea library ready. Questions: volunteer@queenslibrary.org.
notes: A limited number of projects are accepted and a branch must agree to host. Other QPL pages list ages as 14-18 for this program, so check the age limit if you are 18.

name: Queens Public Library Teen Volunteering (ages 14-17)
what_you_do: You can volunteer on library projects in Queens. Roles can be ongoing or one-day events. Hours earn community service credit. You can ask for a Service Verification Letter.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17 with a signed parent consent form. The page says some projects do not require NYS working papers, so check each project's description. Students at schools outside the country or the state may use a waiver.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteer hours count as community service credit.
duration: Varies by project
deadline_text: Minors can apply year-round. Approval and placement can take up to 30 days, longer in summer and fall.
how_to_apply: Get the parent consent form and NYS working papers (from your high school office), create a volunteer account, search projects and click Express Interest/Sign Up, then interview and get an offer letter. Questions: volunteer@queenslibrary.org.
notes: Library says some projects do not need working papers, so check each listing. Working papers take 1-3 weeks from your school, so start early. They are issued regardless of immigration status. Under-14s can only volunteer with a parent or guardian.

name: American Red Cross Babysitting and Child Care Training
what_you_do: You take a Red Cross course on caring for infants and children, safety and emergencies. The online option also covers starting a babysitting business.
who_can_apply: Red Cross says the in-person Babysitter's Training is for ages 11 to 16, and its online Babysitting Basics course is designed for youth 11 and older.
pay_detail: Babysitting Basics Online costs $45 (4 hours, self-paced, certificate valid 2 years). In-person class prices vary by location.
duration: Online course: about 4 hours; in-person length varies
deadline_text: Ongoing.
how_to_apply: Pick a class on the Red Cross Babysitting and Child Care page, or buy the online course there.
notes: The old take-a-class/babysitting-training link no longer works, so the page address was updated. Red Cross says these courses do not qualify you for state-licensed child care. Casual babysitting in a private home does not need a work permit per the California child labor guide (2013 edition).

name: American Red Cross Lifeguard and Water Safety Instructor courses
org: American Red Cross (taught by local pools, cities and YMCAs)
what_you_do: You can take Red Cross courses for lifeguarding or swim instruction. Lifeguard students must be 15 by the last day of class and pass a swimming skills test.
who_can_apply: Lifeguarding: at least 15 years old by the last day of class, plus a swim test (swim, tread water, timed event). Water Safety Instructor and Basic Swim Instructor: at least 15 by the end of the course.
pay_detail: Course fees are set by each provider and are not listed on the pages read.
duration: Lifeguarding: about 27 hours in person, or about 6 hours online plus about 21.5 hours in person
deadline_text: Ongoing. Class dates depend on the provider.
how_to_apply: Use Find a Class on the Red Cross lifeguarding page to pick a pool or YMCA class near you, and check the fee.
notes: Final test is a 50-question exam with an 80% pass mark. Certificate lasts 2 years. Before the update this file said Water Safety Instructor needs age 16; the Red Cross page says 15. For lifeguard jobs, check each employer's page for pay and work permit rules.

name: Red Rock Job Corps Center
org: U.S. Department of Labor Job Corps
what_you_do: Live on campus. You train for a career at no cost. You also earn a high school diploma or equivalent. Training includes human services and collision repair. It includes carpentry and electrical. There are more.
who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules, or have other approved status. You must meet background rules. An Admissions Representative reads your application. This person decides if you can join.
pay_detail: Free to students. The campus page lists furnished dorms, meals, basic medical care, books and supplies, and a living allowance paid in cash twice a month.
duration: Not stated on the pages read
deadline_text: No deadline posted. You start by making a MyJobCorps account on the Job Corps website.
how_to_apply: Create a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Finish the application. Then an Admissions Representative sets up an interview. They review your documents and a background check. They also help you pick a campus.
notes: Mostly fits teens 16 and up who are out of school or want a different path. Housing: dorms are listed on the campus page. A center being listed on the Job Corps site does not prove it is enrolling right now, so confirm with an Admissions Representative. The training list above comes from the center's training page and may not be complete. Whether a state work permit applies was not checked.

name: Redwood City Leaders in Training (L.I.T.)
org: City of Redwood City Parks, Recreation and Community Services
what_you_do: Teens ages 13 to 15 get training. Then they help camp staff with kids at Redwood City summer camps. Activities include group games, sports, arts and crafts and field trips.
who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 15; you must be 13 by the first training day. Written application, then an interview if selected. At most 20 L.I.T.s per session. Redwood City camps.
pay_detail: 2026 fees: $88 for session 1, $98 for sessions 2 and 3, $49 for session 4
duration: 1 to 2 weeks per session
deadline_text: 2026: applications opened April 20 and were due May 8, 2026; interviews May 18 to 21; training June 13. 2027 dates not posted.
how_to_apply: Download the L.I.T. application and email it to tbrent@redwoodcity.org by the deadline. If chosen you interview, then get camp placement and payment instructions. Phone 650-780-5929.
notes: Teens pay a fee to take part (2026: $88, $98, $98 or $49 depending on session). The fee is due after a successful interview. Placement depends on camp needs. A mandatory Saturday training is required. 2027 dates are not posted, so expect a similar April to May window and watch the page.

name: Regeneron International Science and Engineering Fair (ISEF)
what_you_do: It is the world's largest pre-college science fair. You first win a spot at a local fair affiliated with the Society for Science, then compete at ISEF in 22 categories.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12 or equivalent. You cannot enter ISEF directly; you must win at a Society-affiliated fair. Use the Find-a-Fair tool for California fairs.
pay_detail: No entry fee stated on the pages read; more than $7 million in awards and prizes
duration: May 2027
deadline_text: ISEF is in Los Angeles in May 2027 (exact dates not posted on the pages read). Affiliated fairs end by mid-April, and each fair sets its own deadline, so find yours now.
how_to_apply: Use Find-a-Fair on the Society for Science site, then register with your school or regional fair.
notes: Projects can include no more than 12 months of continuous research. The 2027 ISEF is in California, which can lower travel costs for California finalists.

name: Regeneron Science Talent Search
what_you_do: High school seniors submit an independent research project. The top 300 get recognition. The top 40 compete in Washington for awards.
who_can_apply: Students in their last year of high school who live and attend school in the US or its territories, any citizenship. You need your own original research with real data, plus essays, a paper of up to 20 pages, recommendations and a transcript.
pay_detail: No entry fee stated on the pages read; $3.1 million in annual awards, $250,000 first place
duration: Application June 1 to November 5, 2026
deadline_text: Applications close Nov 5, 2026 at 8 p.m. ET (opened June 1, 2026). Top 300 announced Jan 7, 2027; Top 40 announced Jan 21, 2027; finals week Mar 11 to 17, 2027.
how_to_apply: Apply online at the Society for Science application portal (sciencetalentsearch.smapply.org).
notes: Seniors only, so juniors should plan for next fall. Test scores are optional. Homeschooled students may apply.

name: Richmond YouthWORKS Work Experience Program (WEX)
what_you_do: You get a paid internship of up to 100 hours. It is with local businesses, government or nonprofits. You also get workshops and career coaching.
who_can_apply: Richmond youth ages 16 to 21. Must attend required workshops and training to be guaranteed an internship.
pay_detail: Paid internship; the hourly rate is not stated on the page
duration: Up to 100 hours
deadline_text: No deadline stated. The 2026-2027 application is posted.
how_to_apply: Submit the online Work Experience Program application (2026-2027 form linked on the city page). The team contacts you for an intake. Phone (510) 412-2044.
notes: Must live in Richmond. Ask about the hourly wage and your start date at intake.

name: Climate Careers (Green House Calls)
what_you_do: This is a paid job making home energy and water efficiency visits. The visits are called Green House Calls. Then you do an externship at groups such as GRID Alternatives or Berkeley Lab.
who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 24 living in Alameda, Contra Costa, Fresno, Merced, Madera, Napa, San Francisco, San Joaquin, Santa Clara, Sonoma or Tulare county. Must commit to four days a week.
pay_detail: 2026: up to $20.50 per hour for Energy Specialists (up to $22.50 during externship); drivers up to $21.50
duration: Summer; four days a week
deadline_text: No application dates posted. Check risingsunopp.org/jobs for postings.
how_to_apply: Apply through the links on the job posts at risingsunopp.org/jobs/. Phone (510) 665-1501.
notes: As of Oct 7, 2026 the jobs page lists only Central Valley coordinator postings, so no Bay Area summer posting was visible. Pay shown is the 2026 rate. The City of Oakland summer jobs list also includes Rising Sun.

name: Teen Advisory Boards (branch libraries)
what_you_do: At many branches, teens plan library programs and help in the library. They meet during the year.
who_can_apply: Teens at branches that have a board. The page states no age range, so ask your branch.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: Not posted. Contact your local branch.
how_to_apply: Contact your local branch. The page describes no teen application; its online application is for adult volunteers.
notes: Not every branch has a board. The page gives no ages, hours or sign-up steps for teens, so call the branch first. Separate from the City of Riverside Public Library.

name: Library Volunteer (ages 14 and up)
what_you_do: Volunteer at a City of Riverside library branch. Teens 14 and older can apply. Use the City volunteer portal.
who_can_apply: Anyone at least 14 years old who can pass a Department of Justice background check. The library cannot accept court-ordered volunteers.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role
duration: At least 30 total hours at one library before switching
deadline_text: No deadline posted. Apply any time.
how_to_apply: Create an account at riversideca.cervistech.com, find a Library opportunity, click 'Apply to participate', then wait for an email or call. If approved you book a processing appointment with Human Resources at City Hall and get cleared by background check.
notes: This is the City of Riverside library, not the Riverside County Library System. The page does not describe teen-specific roles; it applies to all volunteers ages 14 and up.

name: Leadership Development Program (LDP)
org: City of Roseville Parks, Recreation and Libraries
what_you_do: You get 10 hours of training, then up to 50 hours of job experience helping with summer programs, camps and classes.
who_can_apply: Ages 13 and up. Spots are limited and not every applicant is chosen.
pay_detail: Participants pay a course fee (amount not posted). Includes t-shirt and name tag.
duration: 10 hours of training plus up to 50 hours of job experience training; starts in June
deadline_text: Interest application and recommendation letter due May 5, 2027. Program starts in June 2027.
